stories.title: Bronny James assigned to Coachella Valley Lakers in G League
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have used Bronny James sparingly during their 7-2 start and on Thursday assigned him to their G League affiliate, the Coachella Valley Lakers.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Lakers have used Bronny James sparingly during their 7-2 start and on Thursday assigned him to their G League affiliate, the Coachella Valley Lakers. The 22-year-old third-year guard has averaged just 2.4 minutes and 0.8 points per game in five appearances for the Lakers, who have joined the Portland Trail Blazers (6-1) and Houston Rockets (7-2) atop the Western Conference standings in the early going. James has performed better in the developmental G League, averaging 18.4 points on 49.6% shooting (including 41.3% from 3), 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 25 games the past two seasons for the South Bay Lakers, who were rebranded and relocated this season. The team plays its home games at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, rather than at the Lakers' practice facility in El Segundo. Coachella Valley opens its season Friday at home against the Salt Lake City Stars. Beyond a new home arena, the Lakers' G League affiliate also has a new coach. Alex Cerda was named as the successor to Zack Guthrie after Guthrie joined coach JJ Redick's staff with the Lakers. Lakers rookie Cameron Carr also was assigned to Coachella Valley on Thursday.

stories.detailText: The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders. Quick links: Free agency grades | Trade grades Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz Depth charts | Trade machine | More Nov. 5 Iger's son Will to be part of Lakers' G League broadcast The Los Angeles Lakers' G League affiliate has a new name, a new home, a new coach and a new broadcasting team for the upcoming season. The Coachella Valley Lakers, previously the South Bay Lakers, announced Thursday that Will Iger will be their play-by-play announcer for the upcoming season, with former Lakers big man A.C. Green returning as the color analyst on Spectrum SportsNet. Iger joins Coachella Valley after calling games for the Austin Toros, the San Antonio Spurs' G League affiliate, last season. He has also done studio work for the Dallas Mavericks and play-by-play for San Antonio FC. He is the son of incoming Lakers co-owner Bob Iger and Willow Bay, former co-host of the popular "NBA Inside Stuff" television show with Ahmad Rashad. Coachella Valley will open its season Friday against the Salt Lake City Stars in Palm Desert, California, at Acrisure Arena. It will be Alex Cerda's first game roaming the sideline after being hired in September as CVL's head coach. Cerda served as an assistant for South Bay under Zach Guthrie and was bumped up after Guthrie was added to Lakers coach JJ Redick's staff. Wemby makes MVP opening statement Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain . The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks , becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74. Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961. This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022. "It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often." With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts. "I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there." After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season. Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week. Wembanyama, 22, finished third in MVP voting last season and is seeking to become the award's youngest winner since Derrick Rose in 2011. -- Ben Golliver Nov. 4 NBA Trade Lab updates: Porzingis is popular in mock deals In the first weeks since the release of ESPN Analytics' new NBA Trade Lab , the player involved in the most fan-created trades is Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porzingis , who's in the news because the franchise is withholding payments from him while he's away from the team . With 38-year-old legend Stephen Curry still playing at an elite level, it makes sense that fans want to see the Warriors make a swing to bolster his supporting cast. Add to that how good rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked to start the season, and Warriors fans might be right to think their favorite team isn't that far away from contention in the West, especially considering the early-season injury problems for the Oklahoma City Thunder and Minnesota Timberwolves . Porzingis' $20 million salary would be a key ingredient for the Warriors to match salary in a potential trade. Below are some of the top fan-created trades involving Porzingis, as scored by fans voting from the perspective of each team involved: Trade No. 1 Warriors get: A shot-blocking stretch big in Myles Turner who could be a great fit in their motion-heavy offense to replicate some of Porzingis' game. Milwaukee Bucks get: Porzingis and a young promising player in Moses Moody , who could be more valuable for the Bucks' rebuild. Moody is recovering from a torn left patellar tendon he suffered in March. Trade No. 2 Warriors get: Daniel Gafford , who can provide rim protection and elite play-finishing. He would bolster their center depth and better exploit defenses that are stretched thin out on the perimeter drawn to Curry's gravity. Dallas Mavericks get: Porzingis and a first-round pick swap to help reset their timeline around 19-year-old centerpiece Cooper Flagg , by improving their assets in a potentially loaded 2028 draft. Trade No. 3 Warriors get: Talented 6-foot-8 forward Trey Murphy III , who can defend, draw fouls and rain 3s from well beyond the arc. At 26 years old, he also has the potential to be paired alongside Lendeborg as the wing duo of the future in the post-Curry era. New Orleans Pelicans get: Porzingis, a promising young player in Moody and two future first-round picks to cash in on Murphy's value. Doing this deal would also provide more on-ball opportunities for 2025 lottery picks Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen . Have any more ideas on what move the Warriors should make? Build them in the NBA Trade Lab , then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides. -- Ben Tiemeyer Warriors withholding payments to Porzingis The Golden State Warriors are not making payments to injured center Kristaps Porzingis on his $20 million salary, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Anthony Slater. Porzingis has yet to play a game this season as he continues to deal with recurring symptoms from an ongoing autoimmune condition. Hoop Collective: What does Luka's historic start mean for Lakers? Topics: 1:01: Houston impressing with 6-1 start to season 1:45: Windy Storytime: identifying contenders 4:35: Rockets looking the part of a contender 10:23: Could Kyrie stay with the Mavs all season? 25:10: Injuries stacking up for the Thunder 32:14: Memphis playing quality team basketball 35:40: 76ers winning in clutch time early MacMahon on Kyrie's future in Dallas: "When I'm talking to executives and scouts around the league ... when the Mavericks come up, it is the No. 1 thing people are asking me about. "You know, going into the season, I would have said more likely than not, [Irving] gets moved by the deadline, but I didn't feel super strong about it. The more I see the team, the more I'm around the team, the more I think it's going to be awfully hard to trade him. "Not that there won't be a big market -- there will be, but if they've got a chance to compete for a play-in and playoff spot, I just think it's going to be really tough to move Kyrie. Also, just as much as he means to that locker room and as well as he's working with Cooper [Flagg], it was beautiful basketball. "And just basketball wise they are a phenomenal fit. And I do think there's a legitimate argument to be made for the value of playing meaningful games in March and April for the development of a superstar like Cooper, of young role players like Zaccharie Risacher , who, by the way, is doing some really interesting things -- on the defensive end especially -- and he's got a player option next year. "I think it's a situation where you can get together and handle it in the summer. It's not like you have to either move them or lose them, by this deadline." Oct. 28 How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported. Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington. The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. Already, 2025 first-rounder Will Riley has seen his playing time crater, but he, Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly are all wings who will now likely come off the bench, yet deserve the opportunity to continue their development. -- Zach Kram Haliburton to miss time with hamstring injury Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton will miss time due to a hamstring injury, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Team doctors are now gathering info on a clear timeline of return. Dybantsa had missed the first four games of the season with an ankle injury. What are the Warriors' options on Porzingis? ESPN's Anthony Slater detailed the Golden State Warriors ' options regarding center Kristaps Porzingis and his lingering health issues in a report today. [Stephen] Curry twice made sure to mention the human component, expressing sympathy for Porzingis, who has made public the lingering impact he said he still feels after contracting an upper respiratory viral illness while with the Boston Celtics two seasons ago. "We always said availability was a big factor for our team with all the guys we have out," Curry said. "It's no secret that the [center] spot is an important one for us, especially with his skill set. It's hard to talk about without keeping the humanity of it in mind. But it is a tough one to figure out." Team sources continue to express an extreme level of pessimism that Porzingis will ever play for the Warriors again, but he could end up helping the organization in another way, because his contract, which is only guaranteed for $3 million next season, could still prove to be valuable in executing a trade. Read more: What are the Warriors' options as Kristaps Porzingis remains away from the team? Hoop Collective: Disastrous injuries in OKC, Kawhi out and trouble in Miami Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Bobby Marks to cover the recent injuries to Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace of the Oklahoma City Thunder , including what it means for the team's future and if they will need to make moves to remain a title contender. They move on to the recent injury news to Kawhi Leonard and how it will impact the Toronto Raptors , before closing on the Miami Heat 's 0-4 start and Ty Jerome 's hot week for the Memphis Grizzlies . Topics: 1:35: What does the Thunder front office do now? 18:56: Kawhi to miss time for knee swelling 26:24: How concerned should Heat fans be? 34:59: Memphis much better than expected? Marks on the Thunder's next steps following crucial injuries: "I think the long term, Brian and Tim, is that you will apply for this disabled player exception for Jalen Williams. I don't think you'll get it for Cason Wallace because you have to be deemed out until June 15. And I don't think that Wallace injury will get you there. I think the Jalen Williams injury will. But that doesn't eliminate him coming back. Just because you apply for it doesn't eliminate the player actually returning. That exception will be worth $15 million. You can only sign or trade for a player in the last year of their contract. "Their biggest trade assets are those trade exceptions that were created in the Lu Dort , Aaron Wiggins , and Isaiah Joe trades that range from $17 to, I don't know, $8 million. And you can trade for players on multi-year deals. Now, threshold on this is probably $7 million, right? You're $6.9 below that second apron. I don't think there's an appetite to go in there, but I think there is an appetite to spend because they went out and did that offer sheet on Spencer Jones . That would have added to their payroll another $23 million-$24 million. "So I think that's kind of what you're looking at. You're evaluating guys in that $7-million-to-below range from a roster standpoint, but I also think you can even go north of that if let's say [Nikola] Topic is not going to be a factor this year and he needs to be part of a deal down the road. But that's the long-term picture ... You're basically just trying to hold on right now and then basically figure it out when you get to December." What Edwards' injury means for Wolves On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland. On Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to right knee surgery. Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, 52 games will remain on their schedule. But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue. Edwards to undergo surgery, miss up to two months Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Edwards has been on the injury report for the injury. He dealt with runner's knee in the same leg last season. Leonard out multiple weeks, misses return to LA Toronto Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard will miss multiple weeks due to left knee swelling, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. An MRI showed no structural damage, but the recovery will keep Leonard out of a return game at the LA Clippers on Nov. 2. Topics: 0:32: Jalen Williams injury reaction 14:10: Spurs sending an early message 28:30: Rockets surging out of gate 36:24: Heat struggling at 0-3 42:46: Knicks get headlines for wrong reason 49:24: Brown-Tatum media beef 57:12: Epic scoring performance from Luka Doncic 58:59: Other interesting opening-week headlines Windhorst on what the Jalen Williams injury means in OKC: "I guess I should put my Bobby Marks hat on just because what you want in a podcast is you want analysis of this beyond just a visceral response. The Thunder have the ability to apply for a disabled player exception. But let's be honest here, they cannot replace him." "They'll replace him with what they have on their roster with Ajay Mitchell . He becomes a very important piece right now and the fact that they had to trade away multiple wings over the summer -- Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort ... It comes into play for sure, but this means Ajay Mitchell will have to have a big season and now Cason Wallace , who was just rewarded with a huge contract, those guys will be needed. And you also could see some opportunities for Bennett Stirtz , who actually I think got his first NBA basket tonight. So there's probably no team that could withstand an injury like this other than the Thunder. "They can apply for a disabled player exception, which they will certainly get. They will get, I believe, the full mid-level exception that they can use up to the mid-level exception, which is like, $14-ish million that they can use to to sign a player or trade for a player. They can only trade for a player with that exception who's got one year left on his contract. "They're a very expensive roster. That's one of the reasons why they made those trades. So I cannot see them leaning into that. They're already deep and they're very expensive. So I think it's unlikely they take advantage of that, but there is a mechanism that exists." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 23 Hoop Collective: Luka trash talked and who made an early statement Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to go over the first few days of the NBA season, including Luka Doncic 's night against the Golden State Warriors and the future of Kristaps Porzingis in the Bay Area. Topics: 4:48: Lakers dominate Warriors to start season 6:45: Yaxel vs. Luka back-and-forth getting headlines 11:28: Kessler dream start to career in LA 14:40: Evaluating Clippers first game after punishment 16:50: Will there be punishment for the Bucks from the NBA? 19:08: What is the future with the Warriors & Porzingis? 30:10: Timberwolves impress against the Heat 36:48: After unique offseason Blazers dominate Game 1 40:58: Tough starts for some rookie stars 45:19: Veteran NBA agent Andy Miller joins the show 45:53: A significant move around the NBA 50:58: Windy Storytime: Unique Garnett contract 56:53: Analyzing a unique NBA coaching contract Windhorst on the Gary Trent Jr. situation in Milwaukee: "I will tell you that it is a frequent conversation as I talk with people around the league. You know, they're like, 'Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation? Do you hear anything on the Gary Trent investigation?' It is being done by a different law firm than did the Clippers investigation. They were sort of twin investigations. "I will just say I was talking to an executive the other day and he just said if this was a pre-existing deal and let's just be honest, the word of this deal was out there in the spring. I had an executive say to me that they think, and I want to be clear, I want to be cautious, but I had an executive say to me, if this is proven to be true, then this is actually more egregious than the Clippers deal. When you think of it, the Clippers didn't get any salary cap relief for their salary cap circumvention. They were just funneling their max player more money. In the case of the Bucks, allegedly Gary Trent signed back-to-back minimum contracts and then got this $64 million deal. And over these last two years as they were trying to hang on to Giannis Antetokounmpo for dear life, they got that flexibility that they were able to put into the roster. It didn't work. "Well, I'm just saying if you're going to compare it to Joe Smith ... this is more comparable to what happened with Joe Smith if indeed they are found guilty." Slater on a Porzingis' status in Golden State: "He was around the team in the week leading up to training camp. He went to this event with Jimmy Butler in San Diego, but if you talk to players and people at that event, he wasn't getting on the court. He wasn't in the weight room. He would show up to more of the dinners and the fun stuff. "But it seemed clear right before camp that he was fading away from basketball, obviously dealing with this health issue and thinking about his future. He calls Mike Dunleavy the day before training camp, basically tells him he's not coming in to work, he's going to go deal with this health thing. "He showed up for one meeting two weeks into camp as the Warriors team was in Las Vegas. He met with Mike Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini. From my understanding, those are pretty much the only two he's been communicating with during this entire process. After that meeting, the Warriors announced that he was going to be around the team. Then he left the facility and hasn't returned and has not been around the team to the point that when we put out the report yesterday, the Warriors didn't address some of the trade speculation, but did say he will not be around the team in the immediate future. "Clearly, this is something, as you mentioned, that Mike Dunleavy's called around the league and explored." Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 21 Marks: Warriors have hurdles in a potential Porzingis deal Following the news that the Warriors are exploring deals, finding a trade early in the season for Kristaps Porzingis could be difficult. First, Golden State is hard capped at the second apron and isn't allowed to take back more salary than what is sent out. The Warriors are allowed to aggregate salaries if they are receiving less money in return. Second, since teams are in the evaluation periods of their rosters, trades are uncommon early in the season. Under the current CBA, there have only been two regular season trades in the months of October and November. -- Bobby Marks Sources: Warriors begin exploring trades for Porzingis The Golden State Warriors have begun the process of looking for trades for center Kristaps Porzingis , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Porzingis remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has had him questioning his future with basketball. If there isn't a breakthrough with Porzingis' recovery, stepping away from his career is possible, sources told Charania. Join ESPN's Dave McMenamin for a Reddit AMA! Hoop Collective: Full reaction to the opening-night games Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to react to the NBA's opening day of games, including the Detroit Pistons rallying past the Boston Celtics , the Philadelphia 76ers ruining ring night for the New York Knicks and the Oklahoma City Thunder shutting down Victor Wembanyama in a big win against the San Antonio Spurs . They then welcome Phoenix Suns owner Mat Ishbia to talk about his expectations this season as well as his thoughts on expansion and NBA Europe. Topics: 0:55: 76ers spoil ring night with win at MSG 13:42: Celtics-Pistons reaction 15:14: Detroit dominates second half to beat Boston 21:52: Suns owner Mat Ishbia joins the show 22:49: How the Suns' organization makes big decisions 26:03: Thoughts on possible expansion in the NBA 28:22: Expectations for future of NBA Europe 30:23: State of the Suns for the 2026-27 season 40:26: OKC makes statement in San Antonio Ishbia on the future of NBA expansion: "Well, I'm supportive of growing the game. So I'm pro expansion. "Obviously, it depends on the situation and making sure that it's the right partners because they're now partners with us. And the right value, but also are they doing the right things for the fans? I believe that Vegas is a market that we need to fill. I think Seattle's one. I know there's been talk about Mexico City. The way I look at it is expanding the game. The NBA is a global game. And so having 30 is a limited number. Can you get to 32? I mean, can you go that many more? So, it's like, can you grow? Can you cover a big market like Vegas? "I don't care that it's close to Phoenix. I'm excited. I think there's abundance. There's opportunity everywhere. And I'm supportive of it." Ishbia on the outlook of the 2026-27 NBA season: "First off, there's a lot more balance. The East definitely got stronger. The West is extremely strong. But let's put it aside. "There's also no tanking. So there's not five free wins, eight free wins. And in the East last year, a lot of teams really compounded that because there was about seven teams, six teams trying to lose, which is horrible for our game. NBA Adam Silver did a great job. We got rid of that. So there's no tanking. "People are going to win -- 45 wins is a hell of a season. And I think it's going to be very, very tough. And I think that might be a 4, 5, 6 seed where last year it was 50, 52 wins to get to that level. And so, I think that's not been talked about enough." Topics: 01:08: 76ers Media Day reactions 06:55: How LeBron is assimilating in Philadelphia 15:00: How will the 76ers deploy their talent this year? 18:45: Vibes exceedingly high for the Lakers 32:25: Bronny's quotes about LeBron leaving 35:20: Windy Storytime: Bronny's name origins 40:20: Exciting summer coming to a close for the Knicks 41:15: Major contract negotiations ongoing with NY 55:10: Assessing vibes with new pieces in Minnesota 1:08:40: Bad news continues for the Clippers 1:24:15: Evaluating Kawhi's fit with the Raptors 1:30:20: Not a lot of love in the air for Pistons 1:44:30: Breaking down state of the Warriors 2:00:25: Thunder dealing with departure of key teammates 2:16:13: Interesting quotes from Spurs about their starting 5 Goodwill on the latest between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns: "It wasn't so much what he said, like this full-throated defense of himself, but he said, 'I would like to get my contract done.' "He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up. "And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'" Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Bronny James headed to G League after dismal start to Lakers season
stories.summary: The Lakers assigned Bronny James to their G League affiliate after he saw limited NBA playing time early this season. Here's what to know.
stories.detailText: Bronny James is headed east to California's Coachella Valley, as the Lakers have assigned the third-year player to its G League affiliate. The team announced the move Thursday, and the 22-year-old, along with teammate Cameron Carr, will suit up for the Coachella Valley Lakers, which begin their season on Friday. This follows the Los Angeles Lakers' 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday. James barely factored into the game, logging a single minute. Early on, he hasn't been able to crack regular minutes this season. Through nine games, James has had cameos in five contests with averages of 2.4 minutes and 0.8 points per game. His most recent productive effort came against the Heat when he chipped in two points and a block in a single minute of play. Lakers news: Is this the best version of Lakers star Luka Dončić we've ever seen? Why is Bronny James going to the G League? Bronny James has seen his minutes decrease drastically from the previous season, wherein he logged 6.7 minutes per game over 27 games in his rookie campaign and 8.9 minutes per game over 42 games the following season, 2025-2026. James' father, legendary NBA star LeBron James, is no longer with the Lakers. The 41-year-old is playing for the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year deal with a player option. For the Lakers, the early returns for the roster have been positive. The team is 7-2 and is atop the Pacific Division thanks to inspired play from star Luka Dončić. With eight players averaging 23 minutes or more per game, it's clear James has less opportunity to crack the rotation. The Coachella Valley Lakers open play at Acrisure Arena on Friday, Nov. 6 vs. the Salt Lake City Stars. Whether the game is a precursor to a brief stint or a more prolonged development period remains to be seen. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Bronny James headed to G League after dismal start to Lakers season

stories.title: Portland's Vit Krejci suffers lower leg fracture, expected to miss extended time
stories.summary: The sixth-year pro out of Czechia had been playing a limited role for Portland off the bench.
stories.detailText: When you see the video of the play , it didn't look out of the ordinary for an NBA game. Portland's Vit Krejci was trying to get in front of Phoenix's Miles Bridges and draw a foul in transition, they collided, and Krejci went to the ground grabbing his left ankle. After the game, Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori said Krejci suffered a fracture. After the game, Krejci had his foot in a boot and was on crutches as he left the arena, reports Sean Highkin of the Rose Garden Report . Nori didn't provide details such as which bone was fractured or whether it is in his lower leg or ankle (the team will likely announce that in the next couple of days). Wherever the fracture is, Krejci almost certainly will miss extended time. How much depends on the bone fractured, the severity and the course of treatment, such as whether it requires surgery. Portland acquired Krejci at last year's trade deadline and with the team the 6'8" guard averaged 7.2 points averaging 19 minutes a night through the end of last season. However, with the Trail Blazers getting Damian Lillard healthy and adding Ja Morant this season, Krejci's role shrank, and he is averaging 2.7 points per game in 10 minutes a night. Krejci becomes the third Trail Blazers guard out injured for a considerable stretch, joining Morant (hamstring) and Shaedon Sharp (knee).

stories.title: Development was the plan. So why is Maluach watching from the bench?
stories.summary: The on-off data challenges the eye test, creating a complicated debate about Maluach's minutes and development.
stories.detailText: Oct 21, 2026; Portland, Oregon, USA; Phoenix Suns center Khaman Maluach (10) grabs a rebound during the first half against Portland Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan (23) at Moda Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After yet another double-digit loss on Wednesday night , this time to the Portland Trail Blazers (again), the Phoenix Suns find themselves at 1-5. They are a team desperately searching for an identity. Players are trying to establish defined roles, while the coaching staff continues experimenting with combinations in hopes of finding something that can ultimately translate into success. When you take a step back and look at the bigger picture as it pertains to the Suns’ future, things begin to look rather grim . Between the significant amount of dead cap money on the books and the fact that Phoenix has surrendered control of its draft assets for the next several seasons, there was one thing we understood entering this year that could help keep the franchise competitive: development. After all, continuity and development were the two pillars this organization leaned on throughout the summer. The belief was that returning so many familiar faces would provide a foundation for improvement, while the younger players would take meaningful steps forward in their progression. That was the formula. That was the plan. Yet through six games, the continuity has been noticeably absent, and the opportunities for development have been puzzling. Yes, the organization was forced to adjust its developmental timeline when Mark Williams suffered a shoulder injury in September that required surgery on his left shoulder. Suddenly, the buffer that would have allowed Khaman Maluach to develop behind Williams and Oso Ighodaro in the rotation was gone. The second-year big man out of Duke was now positioned to receive considerably more playing time than the organization likely anticipated entering the season. While that certainly wasn’t the original plan, there was a potential silver lining. Reluctance to play Maluach could no longer serve as an excuse for limiting his opportunities. The Suns were going to need him out of sheer necessity, and that necessity could provide the very developmental experience this organization had spent the summer emphasizing. Those opportunities have certainly presented themselves early on this season. Through the first six games of the season, Khaman Maluach has started all six, averaging 7.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 0.5 steals, and 1.0 blocks in 19.4 minutes per game. The opportunity to develop has been there, but I’ve noticed a troubling trend recently that has me asking one simple question: What are we doing here? Because winning basketball games certainly isn’t what we’re doing right now, and of the many reasons why that’s the case, the minutes being given to Khaman Maluach aren’t anywhere near my top 10. In fact, his absence becomes increasingly noticeable on a team that desperately lacks size and has been horrific at consistently securing rebounds. Phoenix ranks 29th in the NBA in rebounds per game at 39.5 and dead last in rebound percentage at 45.3%. Yet despite those struggles, the Suns continue to limit the playing time of one of the few players on the roster capable of providing a legitimate interior presence. And that brings me to the trend that’s becoming increasingly difficult to understand. In each of the last three games, Khaman Maluach hasn’t played a single minute in the fourth quarter. Against both Denver and Golden State, he was pulled with 7:04 remaining in the third. Against Portland on Wednesday night, his final appearance ended with 6:09 left in the third. Why? Last night against the Trail Blazers, Jordan Ott followed the same substitution pattern we’ve grown accustomed to seeing early this season. Maluach starts the game before exiting midway through the first quarter. He returns midway through the second, plays roughly five minutes, and then starts the second half. But somewhere around the midway point of the third quarter, Ott pulls him from the game, never to be seen again. We’ve now witnessed that exact pattern in four of the Suns’ first six games, and for a team supposedly committed to development, it’s becoming increasingly difficult to understand why. So let’s try to figure it out. Khaman Maluach Substitution Patterns | https://nbarotations.info/player/1642863 Without Khaman Maluach, the Suns are left relying on either small-ball lineups or Oso Ighodaro at the five. And while neither option is inherently problematic, the results have been inconsistent, particularly on the boards. Last night against Portland, Phoenix was actually holding its own on the glass. Yes, the Suns were trailing by 13 points when Maluach exited with 6:09 remaining in the third quarter, but they were winning the rebounding battle 27-25. Over the final 18:09, however, Portland outrebounded Phoenix by 10 and won the offensive rebounding battle 10-5. By the final buzzer, the Trail Blazers had secured a 47-39 advantage on the glass. When Khaman Maluach checked out for the final time with 6:09 left in the 3rd, the Suns held a 27–25 rebounding advantage. Over the final 18:09? Portland outrebounded Phoenix 22–12, including a 10–5 edge on the offensive glass. A 12-rebound swing. That's brutal. pic.twitter.com/Qt10KdRLaE — John Voita, III (@DarthVoita) November 5, 2026 It’s important to note that these numbers reflect the team’s performance before and after Maluach’s final substitution, rather than exclusively when he was on or off the court. The data tells a slightly different story against Golden State. Through the first 28:56, Phoenix had been outrebounded 28-20. But over the final 19:04, after Maluach exited for the final time, the Suns actually outrebounded the Warriors 17-16. Against Denver, Phoenix held a 22-19 rebounding advantage before Maluach’s final substitution, then was outrebounded 21-20 the rest of the way. So what gives? Why is Maluach being banned from the chat after the two-and-a-half quarters of play? Across these three games, Phoenix was outrebounded 72-69 before Maluach’s final departures and 59-49 afterward. That’s a three-rebound deficit becoming a 10-rebound deficit, despite the latter periods being considerably shorter. Welp, we’re done here. It’s clear Ott doesn’t know what he’s doing. But wait. As Rafiki once wisely said, “Look harder…” Rather than evaluating the rebounding numbers based on the point at which Maluach permanently exits the game, let’s examine how Phoenix actually performs on the glass when he’s on the court compared with when he’s sitting on the bench. Against Portland, Maluach played 15:51, during which the Suns were outrebounded 16-12, with the Trail Blazers collecting three offensive rebounds. During the 32:09 he spent on the bench, Portland still held the advantage, though the margin was considerably smaller, 31-27. Phoenix secured 42.9% of the recorded rebounds with Maluach playing, compared with 46.6% when he was off the floor. Maluach Status Team OREB DREB Total On (15:51) PHX 1 11 12 POR 3 13 16 Off (32:09) PHX 13 14 27 POR 13 18 31 Against Golden State, the disparity was even more noticeable. Phoenix was down seven rebounds in the rebounding battle with Maluach on the court and even when he was on the bench. The Suns secured only 36.0% of available rebounds during his minutes, compared with 50.0% when he wasn’t playing. Maluach Status Team OREB DREB Total On (13:18) PHX 1 8 9 GSW 5 11 16 Off (34:42) PHX 8 20 28 GSW 7 21 28 And against Denver? Phoenix was even on the glass with Maluach playing and +2 with him on the bench. The Suns collected 50.0% of recorded rebounds when he was on the court and 51.7% when he was off. Maluach Status Team OREB DREB Total On (17:14) PHX 5 7 12 DEN 5 7 12 Off (30:46) PHX 10 20 30 DEN 7 21 28 Looking at the three games in which Malauch was pulled early, cumulatively, you find that when Malauch was on the court for 46:23, the team was outbounded by 11. Off the court for 97:37? The team was -2. Maluach Status PHX REB OPP REB Differential On Court 33 44 -11 Off Court 85 87 -2 There’s one variable in all of this that we simply don’t have an answer to. We don’t know how Maluach would perform in these fourth quarters if he were actually given the opportunity. We can evaluate what happens during his minutes and compare those numbers with what occurs when he’s on the bench. The numbers certainly complicate the argument that Maluach’s absence is directly responsible for Phoenix’s rebounding struggles. In these three games, the Suns actually rebounded at a higher percentage when he wasn’t on the floor, although the degree of that advantage varied considerably from game to game. That’s an interesting finding, especially given the eye test against Portland, where the Suns appeared to struggle considerably after his final departure. The full on/off data paints a more nuanced picture. Khaman Maluach: Season On/Off | https://hoopsjunkie.io/player/khaman-maluach This is where the conversation becomes particularly interesting, because at what point do you prioritize development over rebounding percentages when a player is on or off the court? Maluach hasn’t looked great to start the season, but he’s certainly been serviceable. And for a team that desperately lacks size, he’s somebody who should probably be seeing a little more playing time at this point. But in the grand scheme of things, when you’re looking at a three-game sample in which the rebounding differential is minus-nine, I don’t believe that’s enough to justify limiting the opportunities and potential growth of a young center who needs experience to develop. Especially when you consider that Maluach has consistently demonstrated a desire to compete and remain engaged. This isn’t somebody whose struggles stem from a poor attitude or a lack of effort. He’s a young player learning how to navigate the NBA, and perhaps we’re overanalyzing a handful of fleeting moments rather than allowing him to work through those experiences. You have to eventually take the training wheels off and let the kid learn, right? Is it too soon? Apparently, the coaching staff believes so. But at some point, the Suns have to decide what they’re actually trying to accomplish this season. If winning is the priority, the results suggest their current approach isn’t working. And if development is supposed to be the foundation for the future, Maluach needs opportunities to make mistakes, learn from them, and grow. Those objectives don’t have to be mutually exclusive. But keeping the training wheels on while the team continues losing accomplishes very little. Especially when the kid is never given a chance to finish the ride.

stories.title: The Lakers are ‘surfing the wave’ of Luka Dončić’s crazy scoring run right now
stories.summary: The Slovenian superstar looks invincible right now
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 30: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers smiles during their game against the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s like déjà vu all over again: Luka Dončić scored at least 40 points and the Los Angeles Lakers rode a vibrant offensive attack to victory. For the fifth time in six games, Dončić eclipsed the 40-point barrier during Los Angeles’ 116-103 win over the Sacramento Kings Wednesday night. The one “hiccup” amid this stretch was a 37-point outing against the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Over that span, the Slovenian is averaging 42.8 points, 8.5 rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.8 steals while shooting 63.3% on 2-pointers, 44.9% beyond the arc (14.8 attempts per game!) and 89.7% at the charity stripe. He’ll rainbow home deep stepback triples, massage his way into crafty, feathery touch shots, draw tons of fouls and still prime teammates for easy shots with one-of-a-kind passing. Every Lakers game is a spectacle hosted by Dončić — and the supporting cast knows it. “You can call it a wave, you can call it a tsunami, you can call it whatever you want,” Walker Kessler told reporters on Wednesday following the Lakers’ third straight win. “He’s scoring the ball. If you want to call it a wave, we’re surfing the wave a little bit when he’s making those shots. I mean he’s incredible.” With 308 points through eight games, Dončić became the first player since Michael Jordan (303 points) in 1988 to tally 300-plus in the first eight games of the season, according to NBA Stats. He also recorded his sixth straight game with at least 35 points, five rebounds and five assists to pass Damian Lillard for the longest such streak in league history. Each night, he seizes control of the action like few others can. In fact, nobody else around the Association can do it like him right now. He is otherworldly dominant and continues etching his name into more rarified company. “You felt it like in that second quarter,” head coach JJ Redick said postgame Wednesday. “I thought, again, we were generating good looks and then he comes down and he makes like three shots in a row that there’s five guys in the NBA can make and all of a sudden the tie ball game is a nine-, 10-point lead. The team feeds off that, too, when he has it going like that.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .
