stories.title: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it
stories.summary: LeBron James took fan interaction to a whole new level on Monday night.
stories.detailText: LeBron James is having fun in Philly and one fan's wine can prove it originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James is one of kind in so many ways. What he did Monday night might be the cherry on top. In the third quarter of the Sixers’ 126-107 victory over the Bulls, James decided he’d take fan interaction to a whole new level. He helped himself to a fan’s red wine. James looked for a transition pass from Tyrese Maxey, who snagged a rebound. James was behind the pass and his momentum took him into the stands, where he disappeared for a few moments. It wasn’t until another angle was shown on replay that we could see what actually went down in the darkness of the seats. James didn’t hold back giving reporters a play-by-play. “I spilled some of his wine,” he said postgame. “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Troy Clemons – the Sixers fan whose drink spilled – explained his perspective on the interaction with James to Kris Rhim of ESPN. “[I was] walking to my seat … LeBron crashed into me, he grabbed me, he said ‘My bad,’ my drink spilled everywhere. He took my drink from me and he basically just took a sip of it, gave it back and ran back on the [court].” Did he keep the cup? “At the end of the day he’s another man like me,” Clemons said. “I mean he’s LeBron, but at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash. And it’s nothing up with him, I just got a fresh drink though.” It should be noted that players are not supposed to drink from fans’ cups, but it’s rare for the NBA to fine someone for a spontaneous interaction such as this. In 2019, a similar thing happened when Mike Scott tumbled into the Bucks’ court-side seats. The Sixers star jokingly took a sip of a fan’s beverage and the NBA opted not to fine him. Time will tell if James has the same fate. If nothing else, an interaction like this just shows how much fun James seems to be having. The 24-year veteran noted the importance of finding joy in the game as he grinds through the season. “It’s a long marathon. And if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working and even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments, these fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well. By playing the game the right way, playing the game hard and then also just being showmen as well, it was a great game for us.” Head coach Nick Nurse also weighed in on the 41-year-old’s mindset coming into the season. “This summer I think he probably stated publicly that he wanted to go some place and have some fun playing. He loves the game, [it’s his] 24th year. It’s a group of guys, like I keep saying, that have been super focused in the intent of playing the right way. I think he’s a big part of that.” The vibes are high. It’s difficult for them not to be. With Monday’s win against the Bulls, the Sixers are 7-1 and lead the Eastern Conference. They’ve won four in a row and the only team they’ve lost to is the Pistons. The Sixers will face them on Wednesday to start a three-game road trip.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown's 30-point night helped the 8-1 Sixers top the Pistons.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers earn strong road win over Pistons, Brown scores 30 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers remain the Eastern Conference’s sole leader. They earned a 112-106 road win over the Pistons on Wednesday night to move to 8-1 on the season and stay at the top of the standings. Detroit fell to 6-2. The Sixers last started 8-1 in the 2023-24 season, which was Nick Nurse’s first as the team’s head coach. Jaylen Brown scored a season-high 30 points and pulled down seven rebounds. Joel Embiid had 26 points and a season-best 15 rebounds. LeBron James posted 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Tyrese Maxey added 19 points and seven assists. The Pistons’ leading scorers were Duncan Robinson with 27 points and Cade Cunningham with 26. The Sixers were down Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pistons’ injured players included Jalen Duren (right hamstring strain) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion). Nurse told reporters in Detroit he thinks “it’ll be another 10 to 12 days before they kind of clear (Barlow) for getting on the court to see where he is,” according to Sixers Wire’s Ky Carlin. The Sixers will visit the Cavaliers on Friday night. Here are observations on their victory over Detroit: Little bit of everything from Embiid in 1st half Embiid assisted the Sixers’ first basket with a sharp pass out of a double team. He saw Brown’s cut along the baseline and dished to him for a layup. Detroit ran several double drag screen actions early, forcing Embiid to defend on the perimeter. The Pistons started 7 for 11 from the floor and took a 17-11 edge on a Robinson three-pointer. The Sixers then made a 10-0 run and Embiid was right in the middle of it. He converted a put-back layup after a pretty high-low feed from James. Embiid hit two foul shots to give the Sixers the lead. The team raised its defensive level and Detroit’s offense grew frigid. Embiid was very good on the glass in the first half, grabbing eight rebounds. The Sixers had an excellent rebounding game as a team, limiting the Pistons to four offensive boards over 48 minutes. Embiid didn’t break out of his early-season three-point shooting slump, going 0 for 3. He’s 3 for 26 (11.5 percent) on the season and hasn’t made a three since the Sixers’ second game. Late in the second quarter, Embiid got into a dead-ball dust-up with Tolu Smith. After an officials’ review, Embiid was assessed a technical foul for “initiating” the altercation. Brown steps up Playing on his 26th birthday, Maxey missed his first four field goals and was scoreless until he hit a floater with 31.5 seconds left in the first quarter. Brown picked up the scoring slack, tallying 10 points in the first on 4-for-6 shooting and hitting a deep, buzzer-beating three to put the Sixers up 29-21. He produced at all three levels, chose smart spots to attack and looked comfortable in the rhythm of the Sixers’ offense. Meanwhile, James did his usuall stellar work as a passer. He assisted two Adem Bona slams in the second quarter and constantly spotted open teammates. Nurse rewarded Bona’s strong opening stint, playing him for a lengthy stretch. Brown swished a corner triple to extend the Sixers’ lead to 48-31. With a 3-for-5 night, Brown is at 45.7 percent from long distance so far this season. It wouldn’t be surprising at all if Brown’s three-point shooting improved from last season’s 34.7 percent clip. With such an abundance of star power, the Sixers’ hope will be that everyone gets regular open looks beyond the arc throughout the year. As for Maxey, he sat with 3:26 left in the second quarter after being whistled for his third foul. Even with a mere two points from Maxey, the Sixers entered halftime holding a 14-point advantage. Sixers stay perfect away from home The Pistons played better basketball to begin the third quarter. Following a John Collins alley-oop jam, Nurse called timeout with his team’s lead down to single digits. The Pistons’ offense sustained some success, but the Sixers prevented a sustained run. Embiid played an especially physical, aggressive third quarter. He tipped in his own miss and Maxey then sunk a three to make the Sixers’ lead 84-68. They were up as many as 17 points in the third. Embiid sat out the fourth quarter Monday night for the Sixers’ win over the Bulls and said he was on a minutes restriction (25) because of his right foot plantar fasciitis. He played the fourth period against the Pistons and logged 33 minutes. Bona went back to the locker room early in the fourth. Nurse told reporters postgame that Bona had “neck soreness.” Detroit did not let the Sixers coast to victory. Robinson drained a three. Cunningham made a pair of free throws and drove in for a layup that cut the Pistons’ deficit to 106-102. The Sixers halted the Pistons’ run before anything disastrous was on the table. Brown blocked a Cunningham three-point try, Embiid knocked down two foul shots, and the East’s No. 1 early-season team improved to 4-0 on the road.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1
stories.summary: The Sixers stayed hot Monday night, reaching 7-1 with a win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bulls to reach East-leading 7-1 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers kept up their hot start to the season Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, reaching 7-1 with a 126-107 win against the Bulls. All five of the Sixers’ starters scored in double figures. Tyrese Maxey posted 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown tallied a season-best 25 points and 11 rebounds. VJ Edgecombe’s 21 points were a new season high. LeBron James recorded 15 points, nine assists and seven boards. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson had 24 points and seven rebounds. Joel Embiid (15 points, eight rebounds) had been listed as questionable with an official designation of “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” He sat out Saturday on the second night of a back-to-back for the Sixers’ win over the Hornets. “Plantar is a little bit of a come and go type of thing,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters pregame. “They’re just trying to manage it. It’s very painful, if you’ve ever had it. It can kind of come and go out of nowhere. So we’re just trying to manage the pain with that, be as smart as we can.” Nurse told reporters that Dominick Barlow is set to see a specialist Tuesday about the back injury that’s sidelined him to start the season. “He’s been on court a little bit … not a ton of moving around,” Nurse said. “I think they want to get to tomorrow’s appointment. Hopefully, it’ll be positive and we can get into his workouts a little bit.” The Sixers will begin a three-game road trip Wednesday when they visit the Pistons. Here are observations on their victory Monday: Edgecombe slamming away off the bat After Embiid blitzed a Bulls pick-and-roll, Maxey picked off Matas Buzelis’ hurried pass to get the Sixers rolling in transition and James jammed home the team’s first field goal. Edgecombe got a slam soon after James grabbed a defensive rebound and the Sixers again pushed the pace. The Sixers scored six quick fast-break points, leading the Bulls to burn an early timeout, and James’ long-distance feeds were a major asset. “If you’re open, he’s going to pass it,” Edgecombe said of James. “The main thing is just being ready. Tonight I had to run and go get ‘em. If you’re open and he sees you, he’s going to pass the ball.” Edgecombe had a dunk-heavy first quarter. He threw down his second when Dean Wade nabbed a steal and dropped off a typically selfless dish to the Sixers’ explosive second-year guard, whose slam put the team up 22-13. The Sixers have an abundance of dangerous options in the open floor, Edgecombe included. As he’s already shown with his continued clutch shotmaking, the 21-year-old won’t become anything resembling a non-factor offensively this year as a byproduct of the Sixers’ enhanced star power. Over the team’s first seven games, Edgecombe had averaged 11.3 points. He scored 11 in the first period on 5-for-5 shooting. More rough minutes for Bona Adem Bona missed a dunk early in the second quarter, which stung a bit more when Jalen Smith drilled a three-pointer seconds later. Bona remained the Sixers’ main backup center. He had a poor first-half stint overall amid a largely negative start to his third season. The 23-year-old big man played well in the Sixers’ victory over the Bucks , posting six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Outside of that, his season has been sparse on bright moments so far. It’s reasonable to wonder when Nurse might turn to alternatives like Jabari Walker, who played a good game Saturday in Charlotte, or try James again at the five. The Bulls outscored the Sixers by eight points in Bona’s first run, cutting their derficit to 40-38. Chicago went in front with a three by former Sixer Buddy Hield. The Sixers regained the advantage late in the second quarter. Maxey and James each were excellent as passers in the first half, combining for 14 assists and three turnovers. James fired the ball to Wade for a corner three that gave the Sixers a 60-52 lead. Sixers outclass Bulls Following a third-quarter Embiid fadeaway jumper and two James lay-ins, the Sixers were up 17 points. The Bulls cut the Sixers’ lead down to 11 points by the start of the fourth quarter. With Bona still struggling and on four fouls, Wade began the fourth at center. Bona then briefly spelled Wade before being whistled for his fifth foul and taking a seat. Embiid ultimately wasn’t needed for any of the fourth period and only logged 25 minutes. Embiid said postgame that he was not available to return to the action in the fourth and has been feeling his plantar fasciitis on the court. The seven-time All-Star’s health is clearly not close to 100 percent. “I was on a minutes restriction,” he said. “(The foot) has been going like that for the past few weeks. It’s painful. Just got to manage it. “If it flares up pretty bad, got to take a step back. We’ve been able to manage it, but it has its ups and downs.” The Sixers’ lead got as low as eight points, but Chicago did not shoot well enough from three-point range (26.3 percent) or have sufficient firepower to sustain a meaningful comeback run. The bottom line is the Sixers are in a different class than the Bulls, who fell to 1-6. As for the Sixers, they’ll wake up Tuesday morning at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. “You’ve got some of these nights where you kind of call them professional wins. …You look at the records and all that kind of stuff, but they have a lot of talent,” Nurse said. “A lot of these teams play a way that’s a little scary. It’s fast and it’s furious, lots of threes. … They’re going to keep coming at you, high-possession games. So they’re not easy games and I’m glad that we handled it professionally tonight.”

stories.title: LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time
stories.summary: James, Philadelphia’s leading facilitator, added a jersey exchange, signature celebrations and a warmup blooper to his latest week.
stories.detailText: LeBron Log No. 3: The King dishes, Caitlin Clark visits and closing time originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia LeBron James’ latest week with the Sixers included his first 10-assist game with Philadelphia, his best performance with the team, a visit with Caitlin Clark, a crowd-wide finger wag and one jumper he would probably like back. Some of it belonged in the box score. The rest quickly made its way around social media. Welcome to the third edition of the LeBron Log. SAFE HANDS Throughout the preseason, the Sixers discussed the responsibility that accompanied their desire to play faster. They wanted to advance the ball before defenses could organize, but Nick Nurse was not interested in accepting extra turnovers as part of the tradeoff. When asked whether he could live with more mistakes if they came with better pace, his answer was simple. “No.” Seven games into the regular season, the Sixers have not yet become one of the NBA’s fastest teams. They entered Monday ranked 20th in pace. Their ball security has stood out. Philadelphia has committed an NBA-low 12.7 turnovers per game. James has helped organize the offense as its leading facilitator, recording 35 assists against 11 turnovers. He leads the Sixers in total assists despite playing only five games. Tyrese Maxey, who has appeared in all seven, is second with 31. James provided the cleanest example Wednesday night against the Pacers. He finished with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, two blocks and no turnovers during the Sixers’ 114-109 comeback victory. It was his first double-digit-assist performance with Philadelphia. According to StatMuse, James also became the oldest player in its database to record at least 10 points and 10 assists while committing no more than one turnover. He was 41 years and 302 days old. James’ night was not flashy by his standards. He attempted 12 shots and finished fifth on the team in scoring. Still, he helped five Sixers reach double figures without surrendering a possession. The Sixers signed the NBA’s all-time leading scorer. Through the opening weeks of his Philadelphia career, he has been their leading passer. CUP BUSINESS James entered his first NBA Cup game with the Sixers possessing more tournament history than anyone else on the roster. He led the Lakers to the inaugural Cup championship in 2023 and was named the event’s first MVP after averaging 26.4 points, eight rebounds and seven assists during Los Angeles’ unbeaten run. Three years later, his first Cup game in red, white and blue produced his best Sixers performance yet . James recorded 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block in Friday’s 98-93 win over the Knicks. He shot 8 for 15 and saved two of his most important baskets for the final 70 seconds. Jalen Brunson’s three-pointer gave New York a 90-89 lead with 1:32 remaining. On the ensuing possession, James backed down OG Anunoby, turned toward the middle and sank a fadeaway to move the Sixers back in front. VJ Edgecombe extended the lead with a three-pointer as the shot clock expired. After Brunson made two free throws, Maxey drove for a layup and missed. James followed the play, collected the offensive rebound and scored the putback with 11.9 seconds remaining. The basket sealed Philadelphia’s second win over the defending champions and its first of NBA Cup group play. “Best game all around,” Nurse said. “He’s been good, but that was his best game for sure.” James has played more than 1,600 regular-season games, but his Philadelphia closing reel has officially begun. LeBron with the clutch tip-in! 👑🔥 The King came through with the finish! 😤 #LeBronJames #EmiratesNBACup pic.twitter.com/S1NLx9l1bm — NBA India (@NBAIndia) October 31, 2026 THE SHRUG AND THE WAG The fourth-quarter baskets were not James’ only memorable moments Friday. After converting an and-one earlier in the game, James broke out his familiar shoulder-shrug celebration. Edgecombe joined him, smiling as he mirrored the move alongside his 41-year-old teammate. The pair had already developed a personalized handshake featuring two taps to the head and a forceful shrug. This one came during the game. James supplied another recognizable celebration in the third quarter. Anunoby drove toward the basket with James trailing the play. James caught him near the rim and was officially credited with his fifth block of the season. He turned toward the crowd and wagged his finger. The fans joined in. Edgecombe later delivered the biggest shot of the game, and James met him with an embrace near the sideline. The two are separated by more than 20 years, but they have quickly developed a collection of celebrations. “He doesn’t shy away from the moment,” James said of the 21-year-old. “Young kid, but he thrives in the moment.” JUST A COUPLE OF HOOPERS James was not the only basketball attraction inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Wednesday. Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark watched the Sixers’ win from courtside and brought a small camera with her. It was the second time this year she photographed James during a game. In March, Clark served as a credentialed photographer when James and the Lakers visited Indiana. “The KING 👑 … Shot by ME,” Clark wrote when she shared those photos. After Wednesday’s game, Clark made her way toward the visiting locker room. She briefly met Maxey before speaking with James in the hallway. James gave Clark one of his No. 23 Sixers jerseys. The team shared photos of the exchange with a fitting caption. “Just a couple of hoopers.” just a couple of hoopers. 🤝 pic.twitter.com/LGHmaBaSit — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) October 29, 2026 Clark publicly expressed hope that James would join the Pacers before he signed with Philadelphia. Their mutual respect goes back further. During Clark’s first WNBA season in 2024, James compared the attention surrounding her professional debut to what he experienced when he entered the NBA directly from high school. “I’m rooting for Caitlin because I’ve been in that seat before,” James said at the time. “I’ve walked that road before.” James did not speak with reporters after Wednesday’s game, so he was not asked about their conversation. Maxey was asked about meeting Clark for the first time. “That’s just another person that I like to watch,” he said. “She cold. She nice. Seeing her today was really cool. Sometimes you try not to fan out, but it was really cool seeing her. It’s her building; she plays here too.” DANCE FIRST, SHOOT SECOND James and Edgecombe also produced the week’s most widely shared Sixers warmup clip. Before Wednesday’s game, the two danced together near the three-point line. Edgecombe moved away while James stepped back and launched a jumper. The shot hit the side of the backboard. Officially the funniest LeBron clip of all time 😭💀 pic.twitter.com/SoGGlO5DAy — FanDuel (@FanDuel) October 29, 2026 The clip spread quickly across social media. James still walked out of downtown Indianapolis with 10 assists, no turnovers and a victory. James has made more field goals than anyone in NBA history. Even the career scoring leader is entitled to one warmup mulligan.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 3-0 Saturday night by beating the Bucks at Xfinity Mobile Arena.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season. Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards. The Sixers’ absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team’s matchup with the Pistons on Sunday. Here are observations on the Sixers’ victory Saturday: Wade debuts, Embiid starts in style Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James’ place. He’d missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain. The 3-and-D forward scored the night’s first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession. Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team’s offense in the early going. The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man. Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead. One of Embiid’s assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter. Second-quarter struggles The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn’t enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter. Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run. Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn’t carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly. Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins’ three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead. The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they’d fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win. The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team’s transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game’s first 19 fast-break points. Star trio produces The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup. Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup. Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks’ odds of a road win. They’d all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter. Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers’ lead to 97-87. The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel’el Ware’s put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee’s deficit to 117-114. The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure. For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

stories.title: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique
stories.summary: They play a brand of unselfish, team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars.
stories.detailText: What makes this 76ers team stacked with superstars so unique originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia They’re a team of superstars that don’t play superstar basketball. That’s the beauty of this 76ers team. They play a brand of unselfish team-first basketball you rarely see from a team loaded with stars. LeBron James is one of the two or three greatest players in NBA history, a four-time MVP, a four-time NBA champion, a 1 st -ballot Hall of Famer. Joel Embiid is a seven-time all-star, a former MVP, an Olympic gold medalist and a likely Hall of Famer. Jaylen Brown is a five-time all-star, an NBA champion, a career 20 points-per-game scorer. Tyrese Maxey is a two-time all-star, one of only two NBA guards averaging 27.0 points per game over the last four years. Four certified megastars on one team. And somehow they’ve figured out how to leave their egos at the front door and play smart, tough, disciplined team basketball, the style of ball you just never see on these superstar-laden teams. On offense, they patiently work the ball around, always looking for the open man or a positive matchup. You’ve got this bunch of big-name, high-priced All-Stars who are just as happy to pass the ball as shoot it. That never happens. The 76ers are sixth in the NBA in assists, and they’re one of only four teams with twice as many assists as turnovers. Smart, unselfish, patient, disciplined. When an all-timer like LeBron averages 7.3 assists per game that speaks volumes. LeBron is fifth in the NBA in assists per game among forwards, which is wild. You can see the joy on his face when one of his passes leads to a basket. When one of the greatest players in history has that mentality, it rubs off on everyone around him. Embiid hasn’t really got going yet on offense and still takes too many 3’s, but he’s also embraced the team-first mentality, and his 4.8 assists per game are more than one full assist above his career average and 4 th -most in the NBA among centers or forward-centers. And still one of the most dominating defensive players in the league. Brown is averaging 27.0 points, which you expect, but he’s also averaging 4.3 assists per game, significantly above his career average of 3.8 coming into the season. He’s fit in so well so fast you forget its his first season here. And what can you even say about Maxey? Just a beast. He’s averaging nearly 30 points per game but never wastes a possession, always makes the right decision with the ball in his hands and is still finding time to average 4.3 assists per game. With James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey, the 76ers are the only NBA team with four guys averaging at least 16 points and 4 assists per game. Only the Pacers, Magic and Raptors have three. But where we’re really seeing this group playing out of their minds is on the defensive end, where this bunch of all-stars, including two newcomers, has been astounding. The 76ers have the 2 nd -best defensive efficiency rating in the league, behind only the Pistons, who they play Wednesday night, and they’re allowing the 2 nd -fewest points in the league, also behind Detroit. Last year, they allowed 123 points per game through eight games. This year they’re at 111. They’re holding teams to 43 percent shooting from the field, 3 rd -best in the league and their lowest since 2011-12. Their 9.3 steals per game are 6 th -most. All five starters are among the top 25 players in the league in defensive rating – James is fourth, Embiid 11 th , Edgecombe 15 th , Maxey 22 nd and Brown 23 rd . How is that even possible? It’s rare to see superstar-caliber guys play as hard on the defensive end as the offensive end. Everybody on this team embraces it. They hustle, they work, they communicate and most importantly they commit to it. The biggest concern when the 76ers built this dream team was that it would be a team of individuals out for themselves, but the reality has been the opposite. In a very short period of time, they’ve learned how to play together. How to play for each other. And we haven’t even mentioned V.J. Edgecomb, who at 21 years old has figured out how to assimilate into this loaded lineup, never force anything, wait for his opportunities and make huge shots when he gets his turn. Edgecombe is at 12.7 points and 3.0 assists per game, and his numbers are understandably down a bit from last year, but if that bothers him it sure doesn’t show. And the role players – Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Jabari Walker – have each adopted the same ego-free style of basketball, supporting the starters however they need to. Nick Nurse deserves a ton of credit for getting this bunch to play this brand of hoops. It’s not easy to get any NBA player to put team goals ahead of individual goals. But he’s got Hall of Famers and all-stars doing it and having a blast along the way. They all seem to love playing basketball the right way and they seem to love playing together. The 76ers are 7-1 and looking like a real threat to win the East, and they’re doing it by playing the game the right way. By committing to each other and not themselves.

stories.title: Can the Suns fix this from within?
stories.summary: Defense, rebounding, chemistry and player roles are all creating problems for a Suns team searching for answers.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 02: Jalen Green #4 of the Phoenix Suns reacts after he was called for a foul on Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors in the second half of their game at Chase Center on November 02, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not great. Some people would pick less euphemistic words, but I’m trying to be nice. I’ll admit I didn’t envision this happening. I never expected the Suns to be world beaters, but I also didn’t expect them to be a punching bag as they stumbled out of the gate. The most glaring deficiency with the Suns through the first six games is defense. The Suns are second to last in points per game allowed, behind only the Chicago Bulls, at 124.3 points per game. After a bleak 1-4 start, they surrendered a season-high 132 points last night when they knew this was a critical match to right the ship. The Suns are dead last in Defensive Rating, allowing 125.6 points per 100 possessions. The Suns need to find a lineup that can get stops. That should be the main priority in practices. Switch people around and try to get something to click. Switch people around in the games if they aren’t giving maximum effort. I’m fine with anybody sitting down and watching what effort looks like. Sometimes it appears the Suns struggle with fundamentals like switching or fighting over screens. Effort, strategy, and execution. One hand needs to know what the other is doing. Someone I went to the game with last night, who isn’t a basketball aficionado, said it just seemed like Portland was scoring so fast and easily. I guess you don’t have to be a basketball genius to see the Suns suck at defense right now. She said the Suns also missed a lot of threes. The Suns could have been better. They shot 10-of-36 from deep for a 27.8% clip. Maybe if another two or three of those went in when the Suns were trying to close the gap, things could have turned out a little differently. I told her that, the way I look at it, three-point shooting is mostly something that improves with practice. It’s not like defense, where if a player gives maximum effort, their performance can improve in real time. Effort doesn’t affect shooting in the same way it does defense. A lot of defense is effort, and the Suns aren’t meeting the standard they set last season. I have always considered defensive rebounding as part of defense. That word in front of rebounding is the hint. A defensive rebound ends an offensive possession, and ending the opponent’s possession is important. Portland snatched 16 offensive rebounds against the Suns, who are relinquishing the third-most offensive boards in the league at 14.5 per game. Boxing out might help. I hope they realize that because they are not doing it. The Suns need to rebound by committee. Khaman Maluach is leading the team in rebounds per 36 minutes with 11.2, but other holes in his game prevent him from being a true anchor at this early stage. Last season, Mark Williams was second on the team in rebounds per 36 minutes, and Jordan Goodwin was sixth. Goodwin was also second in defensive rating. Getting these guys back could definitely have a positive effect, but for the Suns to turn this around, they will need to ramp up effort. This isn’t just a scheme issue. Where is the continuity, chemistry, and…. joy? The Suns have 10 players averaging over 10 minutes a game this season. Of those 10, eight were teammates on the Suns last season. Only Miles Bridges and Luke Kennard are being incorporated into whatever system the Suns are attempting to run. This year the Suns don’t look like they dislike each other, but they don’t have the same energy. One possible cause of the perceived chemistry issues is that Jalen Green is being asked to play a different role, more as a distributor. Unfortunately, through six games, he is averaging just 3.3 assists, which is exactly his career average. The Suns are now 18-20 in regular-season games when Green plays. 18-24, counting the bloodbath at the hands of the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Suns might be trying to shift from Point Book to Point Green, but right now it looks like an experiment with less-than-impressive results. Sometimes I think it might just be easier for the Suns to get a real point guard. Then other players would be freed up to exploit their strengths. This happened when Chris Paul played with Devin Booker, and they had a decent run, but that isn’t this roster. Ott needs to determine who is best equipped for this role, since there isn’t a perfect fit. If it is Green, then Jalen needs to figure this out fast. The clock is ticking. If it isn’t Green, then Ott needs to figure this out fast. The clock is ticking. The Suns have a problem in the middle. I may have softened a little in the midsection as I’ve gotten older, but the Suns’ underbelly is softer than an armadillo’s. The problem is the Suns don’t have a protective shell. They are just kind of soft overall right now. Maluach looks like the game is entirely too fast for him at this stage. By the time he sees where he needs to be, the play has already evolved past the point for him to get involved. Maluach has obvious talent, but his positioning needs a lot of work and… he has hands of stone. Oso Ighodaro is averaging 4.3 assists per game and has demonstrated the ability as a playmaker to find cutting teammates for easy baskets, but he lacks the size of a true big man and will be at a disadvantage almost nightly. The Suns need to rebound as a team. Last season Mark Williams was second on the team in rebounds per 36 minutes, and Jordan Goodwin was second. Goodwin was also second in defensive rating. Getting these guys back could definitely have an effect, but for the Suns to turn this around, they will need to ramp up effort. This isn’t just a scheme issue. Can the Suns fix this from within? I don’t know. The optics have not been encouraging. There are things that we should at least hope to see. 1. Find a lineup that clicks defensively. Practice overall schemes and implement changes specific to the opponent. Players need to give maximum effort or keep the bench warm for someone who will. Maybe Jordan Goodwin’s return will help, but this needs to happen immediately. This should be attainable. Since the team is essentially worst in the league they could still be “terrible”, as Dillon Brooks described… and improve. 2. Figure out the rotations and how this offense actually needs to flow. The numbers here aren’t as pitiful as the defensive side, but the Suns are 26th in the league in pace, averaging only 97.3 points per 100 possessions. They are slow and constantly look disjointed. I can watch a losing team play basketball, but bad, boring basketball is a big ask. 3. Get Mark Williams and Jordan Goodwin back. The Suns’ injuries are exposing their weaknesses. Defense and rebounding are the biggest culprits for this start, and those are the main things those two bring to the table. Right now nobody is eating at that table. The Suns are better equipped to suffer an injury at other positions. The Green/Brooks/Booker combo should actually give good insurance with some overlapping skills. Those two wouldn’t make this team 5-1 right now, but anything would help. 4. Find a way for Booker to be a better version of himself. If Booker just plays like a good player, and not an elite All-NBA type of player, this team probably won’t make the playoffs. Steve Nash won MVP in Phoenix at 30, but Booker is not passing the eye test at the same age. 5. Try harder. Please make the fans think the players want to win as bad as the fans do. 6. Prayer. If any of you are religious or spiritual, it couldn’t hurt. 7. Jordan Ott’s honeymoon is over. Time for the part of marriage that takes a lot of work. Hopefully Ott and the players are ready to commit. Hopefully Ott is up to the challenge. He has an imperfect roster and he has to get players in their best roles to succeed…. even if he hurts someone’s feelings. If these things don’t happen, it might be a long season… or potentially short for the people who can’t stomach it.

stories.title: JJ Redick was impressed with the Lakers’ defense after flat start vs. Kings
stories.summary: Redick enjoyed how his team fared over the final 3.5 quarters on Wednesday
stories.detailText: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 02: Head coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the third quarter of the NBA game against the Miami Heat at Crypto.com Arena on November 02, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second straight game, head coach JJ Redick praised his team’s defensive performance following a sluggish start. In the Los Angeles Lakers’ win over the Miami Heat on Monday, Redick complimented their second-half showing , when they limited Miami to 45 points and a 95.7 defensive rating. On Wednesday, he was pleased with how they responded after the Sacramento Kings raced out to 16 points in the opening 4.5 minutes. Ultimately, the Lakers bounced back for a comfortable 116-103 victory and moved to 7-2 on the young season. “I think when the game started, we were a little flat. I called an early timeout. They had 16 points. They scored 87 for the last 43:27 seconds or whatever it was [after] I called that timeout,” Redick said postgame. “The promising thing on that side of the ball is the effort and the intent to execute, I think, is really high. Second efforts were really good. We had a number of veer switches and peel switches and scrambles, had a number of late shot clock possessions for them, some shot clock violations. We did a lot on that end. I think the activity overall was really good, save for the first four minutes or whatever it was.” Against the Kings, Los Angeles posted a 105.1 defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass, which marked its third-stingiest effort of the season behind an Oct. 28 win over the Los Angeles Clippers (90.9 defensive rating) and an opening night romp of the Golden State Warriors (96.5). The Lakers’ defensive anchor, Walker Kessler, is pleased with certain aspects of their play but still sees areas to refine as the year progresses, particularly in the open floor. “We got to clean up some stuff on the defensive end,” Kessler said Wednesday. “Our half-court defense, once we get set, is pretty good. Got to do better in transition as a collective.” While the Lakers allow the seventh-fewest points per 100 transition possessions (113.2), they allow the sixth-highest transition frequency (16.9%). Thus far, that inability to slow teams is really bogging them down. Despite being seventh in transition defense and eighth in half-court defense (91.3 points per 100), they’re just 16th in overall defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. Despite Ja Morant’s absence, they’ll face a stiff test in their rematch Friday against the Portland Trail Blazers, which own the league’s top-ranked offense and sit top five in both half-court and transition efficiency. Tipoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. inside Crypto.com Arena. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

teamStories.summary: The Dallas Mavericks know they must get off to better starts going forward if they want to win big games consistently.
teamStories.detailText: For 24 minutes on Wednesday night, the Dallas Mavericks looked like a team with more questions than answers. For the next 24 minutes, though, they looked like a team that had found a winning formula against the reigning Western Conference champs. Despite rallying back from being down 19 points in the second half to take a late three-point lead, the Mavs ultimately came up short in a 112-111 loss to the San Antonio Spurs on the road. The second consecutive loss dropped Dallas to 4-4 on the season. It’s also the Mavs’ second loss to San Antonio in less than two weeks, after the Spurs rolled to a 122-106 win in Dallas on Oct. 24 with Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving both sidelined. This one had a different feel, though. Despite Victor Wembanyama going off for 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks, the Mavs still had an opportunity to win the game at the end, but Irving’s last-second shot just wouldn’t drop. As encouraging as it was to see the Mavs not give up and fight back to make it a close game, nobody seemed happy to come away with any moral victories on Wednesday night. “I feel like it’s a bad thing,” Naji Marshall said when asked what it meant to come back from 19 down. “I feel like we’re kind of telling ourselves and showing ourselves personally what we’re doing wrong. I feel like we’re letting ourselves down. Just practice what we preach. Go out there from the jump and play like [how we did in the second half]. Who knows how the game will turn out?” Irving also spoke about the Mavs’ uninspiring first half. San Antonio put up 32 points in the first quarter and 36 more in the second, and Dallas spent most of that stretch, in his words, “playing on our heels.” “We just got back to the identity that we’re trying to build for ourselves, which is, you know, it’s not so much desperation basketball, but it’s just playing to be the hunters,” Irving said. “… They were getting a lot of offensive rebounds, a lot of second chances. … The second half, I feel like we hit them and they had to respond, and that’s what got us back in the game.” Instead of driving into Wembanyama at the rim, the Mavericks made a big adjustment and started kicking the ball out, re-spacing and letting it fly. Dallas ended up shooting 14-of-37 (37.8 percent) from deep. “We stopped challenging Wemby at the rim, and started making better decisions with the basketball,” Mavs head coach Dusty May said. This isn’t the first time the Mavericks have had to dig out of an early hole this season, and they know that’s a problem that needs to be addressed if they want to potentially be a playoff contender this year. “To start off the game and, you know, give two quarters up, 32 and 36, that’s not where we want to be,” Irving said. “And when you’re giving up that amount of points in the first half, teams are going to be very comfortable and you got to work your way back. … I think we have to start trending in a direction where we’re going into halftime with a lead.” The good news, though, is that the Mavericks now have proof of what that version of themselves looks like. May and the rest of the guys will now just have to figure out how to make it show up from the opening tip more consistently. Dallas will be in action again on Friday at American Airlines Center against the 1-7 Utah Jazz. The game will tip off at 7 p.m. CT. It will be the Mavs’ second NBA Cup game of the season. They won their first NBA Cup game against the Houston Rockets last week, improving to 1-0 in Group Play.

teamStories.summary: Victor Wembanyama had career highs of 52 points and 24 rebounds along with eight blocks to power the Spurs past the Mavericks on Wednesday night.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- Victor Wembanyama earned the polyphony of MVP chants that vibrated through Frost Bank Center by cramming a full night's work into his first 17 minutes before finishing with career highs in points (52) and rebounds (24) in the San Antonio Spurs ' 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. "It's just figuring things out," Wembanyama said. "Sometimes, you're one step ahead. Also, I haven't been feeling great lately. I'm sick. I felt like I got my legs back. So, it should be more like this more often." If so, beware to the rest of the NBA. Wembanyama started red-hot against the Mavericks, racking up 10 of San Antonio's first 12 points on the way to pouring in 29 points over nearly 17 minutes in the first half. The outburst was his second-highest scoring output in any half in his career, eclipsed only by his 37-point first half in February against the Los Angeles Lakers . More than half of the points (15) came at the foul line, with Wembanyama nailing all 15 of his free throws to tie James Harden in 2019 for the most without a miss in the first half during the play-by-play era (since 1997-98). Wembanyama logged 15 rebounds and five blocks in a first half that San Antonio led 68-51. The 22-year-old made history by becoming the first player to record at least 25 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks in a half. Wembanyama finished with eight blocks, the most in a 50-plus-point performance since blocks became official in 1973-74. "Twenty-[four] rebounds, nine offensive rebounds," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "Excluding the 3s, he was 15-for-20 from the field, which means he was all over the basket area and around the paint. He was a man tonight, and his teammates rewarded him quite a bit. He got rewarded in a variety of ways by just dominating both ends." Wembanyama became the first player with at least 50 points and 20 rebounds in a one-point win since Wilt Chamberlain in 1964 and just the third player in NBA history with such a line, also joining Elgin Baylor. He is the fifth player in NBA history with multiple 50-point games at age 22 or younger, having put up 50 in a win over the Washington Wizards in November 2024. Told that Wembanyama's stat line was comparable to Chamberlain's performances of the past, Spurs guard Dylan Harper didn't mince words. "He's basically Wilt," Harper said. "The other team tries to do everything [to stop Wembanyama]. They throw out any adjustment, every adjustment. It's hard to keep big fella out of the paint. He's so dominant when he screens and rolls. He knows how to get to his spots. He's great at the free throw line. So, for us, it's just how do we get him the ball and how do we get the low man away from him?" Wembanyama also drew comparisons to another Hall of Famer -- he joined Bob McAdoo in 1974 as the second player since blocks became official with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in a game. Perhaps the most eye-popping portion of Wembanyama's virtuoso performance took place on the defensive end. Over a span of 13 seconds in the second quarter, Wembanyama swatted away three consecutive shots from Cooper Flagg , P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford in the same possession. Flagg tried Wembanyama first with an eight-foot floater that the Frenchman smacked into the crowd opposite Dallas' bench. Then, Wembanyama blocked Washington's pull-up attempt into a group of fans behind the Mavericks' basket. Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox collected the third block of the sequence. "If I got blocked three times in a row, I feel like I'd be pretty upset," Harper said. "But that's Vic. He takes pride on the defensive side and things like that are just natural to him." Dallas shot a combined 2-of-13 in the first half when contested by Wembanyama, with the average field goal distance coming from 5.5 feet. With 9:11 left to play, Wembanyama and the Spurs experienced somewhat of a scary moment when he rolled his right ankle. Wembanyama subbed out with the Spurs leading 94-87. Once the Mavericks cut the deficit to one point (100-99) with 6:05 left on a Flagg alley-oop dunk, Wembanyama reentered to close out the game with 10 points down the stretch. "He's Superman," Harper said. "He rolls his ankle and pops right up and acts like nothing happened. I've never seen [something] like that, but that's a testament to how he takes care of his body." Wembanyama said he was "feeling fine" when asked about the sore ankle, calling the play "the moment that stands out" because "both teams were really fighting at this moment, and they stepped up their physicality and forced us to step up ours." No player has produced more points, rebounds or blocks in a game this season than Wembanyama, who tied or set NBA highs in all three categories against the Mavericks. San Antonio outscored Dallas 87-64 during Wembanyama's time on the floor but struggled to a minus-22 when he was on the bench. "I think he's settled into the season like we all have," Johnson said of Wembanyama. "We just had to make sure we got to a good spot in terms of this team needed to get to where our feet were. There's a lot with this team that has potential and there's a lot this team had to get to the starting blocks for the season. We're starting to finally play the brand of basketball that we know how and how we should play." ESPN Research contributed to this report.

Open Thread: Tracy McGrady says Kevin Garnett was more impactful than Tim Duncan
teamStories.summary: David West jumps in on the conversation via social media
teamStories.detailText: Basketball: Closeup of San Antonio Spurs Tim Duncan (21) and Boston Celtics Kevin Garnett (5) during game at AT&T Center. San Antonio, TX 3/17/2008CREDIT: Greg Nelson (Photo by Greg Nelson /Sports Illustrated via Getty Images)(Set Number: X79837 TK1 R1 F342 ) On their podcast, Cousins , 2000 NBA Slam Dunk Champion Vince Carter and and 2001 NBA Most Improved Player Tracy McGrady discuss a variety of NBA topics. The cousins (it’s not just a clever name for a podcast though it is not a show hosted by Boogie Cousins, as I mistakenly originally believed) discovered their familial bond at a reunion. They played together with the Toronto Raptors a year later. Both had significant NBA careers. Tracy McGrady finished his career with the San Antonio Spurs as part of the 2013 title run. He recently posited that though Tim Ducan is considered the greatest power forward of all time, he thinks it is a benefit of how Duncan was able to design the Spurs around him. The idea is put forth that Kevin Garnett did more than Duncan, but the titles make Duncan look the better player. It was Tim's system. One thing I realized my year with them was that Tim built the damn thing. It was his brainchild. It was his basketball genius that made that shit the monster it was. IYKYK 🤷🏽‍♂️ https://t.co/kmcobX6Ihi — David West (@D_West30) November 4, 2026 My initial reaction was to defend Duncan and dismiss McGrady as having an axe to grind or something. But after listening, I have to give him some respect. McGrady clearly states that he “look(s) at the game totally different.” I cannot begin to imagine the wealth of basketball knowledge, a conversation most assuredly to float above my head and waft ad the words left his mouth. The repost from David West puts it into perspective. It was Tim’s system. One thing I realized my year with them was that Tim built the damn thing. It was his brainchild. It was his basketball genius that made that shit the monster it was. IYKYK 🤷🏽‍♂️ It opens up the conversation. Could Tim Duncan have become the Tim Duncan of the Spurs if he had been drafted by the Boston Celtics? What about if he had left San Antonio to play in Orlando? If the environment changes, doesn’t the payer change in some form or fashion? If Kevin Garnett had been given the keys to the kingdom of Minnesota? Or been drafted first overall by Golden State (hindsight being 20/20 and all), could he have cultivated an organization than won five championships? As a Spurs fan, I am fortunate those are just questions. Tim Duncan was drafted by the Spurs, decided to stay after considering Orlando (if Doc Rivers could go back he’d give Duncan his own private jet…hindsight being 20/20 and all), and completed a nineteen year career in San Antonio bringing more than five championships to the city. He brought a culture, and a style, and a temperament that embodies the franchise’s personality. And now we Victor Wembanyama. The most talented player of his generation, a genuine gentleman, a scholar, and a player who carries some of the great qualities that have already been associated with the Silver & Black. Honestly, McGrady’s take doesn’t bother me at all. I’ll take what we’ve got. Welcome to the Thread. Join in the conversation, start your own discussion, and share your thoughts. This is the Spurs community, your Spurs community. Thanks for being here. Our community guidelines apply which should remind everyone to be cool, avoid personal attacks, not to troll and to watch the language.

stories.title: Jonathan Taylor turns trade talk into 'regular scheduled programming' as Colts and Cowboys meet
stories.summary: — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins. This week, he has heard his named linked to multiple teams, heard about “done deals” and heard some question whether it's wise to even play Sunday when the struggling Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys meet — two days before this season's trade deadline. So Taylor has learned how to laugh it off. All he wants to do is give the fans something to cheer. “It's kind of dragged on for a while now, so at this point, it's just noise,” Taylor said Thursday about the chatter. “It's been like three or four or however many weeks, so at this point, it becomes regular scheduled programming.” It wasn't supposed to be this way after the seven-year veteran who has never played for another team signed a two-year contract extension worth $44 million to stay with the Colts in August. Even then, this week's featured matchup was supposed to be about the brother bash: Indy's veteran receiver Josh Downs and Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs . But with both teams reeling, the older brother requesting a trade and the younger brother in the concussion protocol and dealing with a bad ankle, their dream story may have to wait. That puts the spotlight on Taylor, the franchise's No. 2 career rusher in what could be his final game playing in the Colts — though it's not something he has contemplated. “We've got an opportunity, especially this week — especially after last week — to come back and put a better product on the field,” he said, referring to the embarrassing 42-7 loss to Jacksonville. “That's my biggest goal. Last week was tough. You know you never want to go and put that on display." He just wants to give fans something to cheer about. Indy has (2-6) lost four straight and 13 of 15 and the last time they were home, the boobirds were out in force. Dallas (3-5) hasn't played much better lately. It has the league's worst run defense and has lost three of four after blowing a lead and losing 33-30 in overtime at Arizona last week. So coach Brian Schottenheimer would like nothing better than to ruin Indy's homecoming — even if it Taylor's last stand. “There are certainly a lot of things we as a football team can do better," he said, noting the Cowboys' rushing disparity from Week 7 to Week 8. “I didn’t think we did a great job tackling. And then there’s certainly things that I can do better in all facets, No. 1 being find a way to finish the game and give us a chance.” Need to know Dalals (3-5) at Indianapolis (2-6) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: Cowboys by 5½. Against the spread: Cowboys 4-4; Colts 4-4. Last week: Cowboys lost to Cardinals 33-30 in OT; Colts lost to Jaguars 42-7. Last meeting: Cowboys beat Colts 54-19 on Dec. 4, 2022, in Dallas. Series record: Cowboys lead 11-6. Matchup to watch Cowboys pass defense vs. Colts QB Daniel Jones . With the uncertainty around Taylor after a season-low eight carries last week, the more determinative matchup may be the turnover-prone Jones against a team ranked in the bottom five in takeaways (six). Jones has lost four fumbles, thrown nine interceptions and has at least one INT in seven games this year. Stats and stuff — The Colts and Cowboys faced each another three times before the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, then met again in Super Bowl 5, a 16-13 Colts victory when the team was still in Baltimore. — Dallas has only one win outside Texas this season. It came at Philadelphia in Week 6. — WR CeeDee Lamb is one of three players entering Week 9 with 60 catches and he became the first player in franchise history to reach that mark in eight games or fewer. — QB Dak Prescott has thrown at least one TD pass in every game this season, a personal best streak to start a season. — Indy is playing at home for the first time since general manager Chris Ballard was fired and Pro Bowlers Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded. — WR Keenan Allen needs four catches to pass Tim Brown for No. 8 on the NFL's career list. Brown had 1,094 during during his Hall of Fame career. Allen has 29 catches in his last five games. — Taylor ranks eighth in the NFL in yards rushing (610) and is tied for third with eight TD runs. — Indy is tied for last in the league in takeaways (four) and has the worst turnover margin at minus-11. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts
stories.summary: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts.
stories.detailText: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court Wednesday, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts, according to federal court records. Rice, who filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, claimed more than $2.1 million of his debts are tied to varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations that have either been settled or are awaiting trial. Rice, 26, has been sued by multiple individuals for his role in a high-speed multicar crash in Dallas in 2024 and an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025. In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in "deferred compensation." The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property. Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for "individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors," according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt. The documents claim Rice's largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit. According to the documents, Rice used his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral with Thomas McMurray, his attorney in the pending civil litigations. Rice's bankruptcy attorney, David Shuster, and the Chiefs had no comment about the bankruptcy filing. McMurray did not immediately respond to messages left by ESPN seeking comment. Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract with the Chiefs and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026. He has played in five games this season, with 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.detailText: Malik Nabers | Getty Images New York Giants wide receiver M alik Nabers , the NFC Offensive Player of the Month , missed practice on Thirsday with a knee issue. Running back Cam Skattebo missed his third straight practice on Thursday, increasing the likelihood that Skattebo will miss Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles due to a hamstring injury. Nabers missed most of the 2025 season after suffering a torn ACL. Nabers told media after practice that he would “ be good ” for Sunday. You have to believe this is a game Skattebo would very much like to play in. The Giants will be at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, the place where Skattebo suffered his season-ending ankle injury in 2025. Getting that opportunity might not, though, be in the cards for Skattebo. If Skattebo can’t play, Devin Singletary and Gregory Desrosiers are on the 53-man roster, and Phil Mafah and Eric Gray on the practice squad. “It’s going to be the utmost importance to keep the run game going,” offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said on Thursday. “You can’t be one dimensional and just be dropping back, throwing. You’ve got to be able to keep that run game going. So, no matter who’s back there with the carries, we’ve got to be efficient with the run game.” Star edge defender Abdul Carter returned to practice after sitting out Monday and Wednesday due to an illness. Charlie Jones, the Giants’ primary kickoff and punt returner as well as being a backup wide receiver, practiced on a limited basis with a hand injury. That is concerning for a player who has to catch and protect the ball. stories.title: Ravens officially place Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley on IR with thumb, turf toe injuries
stories.summary: Baltimore also activated former UFL quarterback Austin Reed to the 53-man roster after signing him earlier this week.
stories.detailText: The Baltimore Ravens will officially be without their top two quarterbacks for the near future: The team announced Thursday that it has placed both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve . The Ravens also activated UFL quarterback Austin Reed to the 53-man roster after signing him earlier this week . Reed will be the backup for undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who is set to make his first career start on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. We have signed QB Austin Reed to the 53-man roster and placed QBs Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve. We have also elevated OLB Adisa Isaac and kicker Jake Moody from the practice squad (standard elevations) for tonight’s game. — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) November 5, 2026 Jackson injured his thumb during Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Baltimore's first offensive play. Jackson was making his return from a three-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, and he got injured on his first throw since Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Bills linebacker Greg Rousseau made contact with Jackson's hand while attempting to defend the pass, and Jackson immediately walked off the field and into the Baltimore locker room. The Ravens quickly ruled him out of the rest of the game with the thumb injury. Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson would require surgery on his injured thumb and a stint on injured reserve. The Ravens did not reveal Sunday the precise nature of Jackson's injury, only that he had injured the thumb on his throwing hand. Asked at the time if the injury was season-ending, Minter said, "We'll see ." Huntley, meanwhile, was diagnosed with a turf toe injury that is reportedly season-ending . Huntley, a career backup, started three games this season while Jackson was out with the ankle injury. The injury is a critical blow for the Ravens and Jackson, whose recent seasons have been marred by injury. Jackson's a two-time MVP and one of the game's best players when healthy. When Jackson's available, the Ravens are regularly considered Super Bowl contenders. Still, help is reportedly on the way, with Baltimore reportedly acquiring Jacoby Brissett in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals. The trade will reportedly not be completed until this weekend, meaning that Brissett cannot start for the Ravens on Thursday; he is reportedly expected to be the starter in Week 10. How will injuries impact Jackson's contract talks? Both leg and back injuries sidelined Jackson for four games in 2025 and limited his play in others. The result for the Ravens was a disappointing 8-9 campaign that fell short of the playoffs. Jackson missed five regular games in each of the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Including Sunday's game in which he played just one snap, Jackson has missed a total of 21 games since his rookie campaign in 2018. The 4-4 Ravens now face another season of fighting for a playoff spot with their MVP quarterback on the sideline. The injury arrives at a critical juncture in Jackson's career as he is on the fourth year of a five-year, $260 million contract. Team owner Steve Bisciotti has expressed his desire to make Jackson a Raven for life, but the two sides reportedly haven't engaged in substantial contract negotiations . Now those contract talks and decisions will take place in the context of another of Jackson's seasons significantly limited by injury.

stories.title: The Packers are asking Jordan Love to do something historically difficult
stories.summary: With an impotent rushing attack and a league-leading number of drops, Jordan Love is being asked to carry a pretty one-dimensional Packers offense.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) Jordan Love is putting together one of the best seasons of his career. That’s good timing, because the Packers aren’t making things particularly easy on him. Through eight games, Love leads the NFL with 2,246 passing yards and has thrown 16 touchdowns. He’s on pace for a franchise-record 4,772 passing yards, potentially surpassing Aaron Rodgers’ 2011 season. But there’s a caveat: Love is being asked to overcome problems that few quarterbacks could reasonably be expected to sustain. The Packers are averaging just 60.6 rushing yards per game, the lowest mark in the NFL over the past decade. They’re also responsible for 23 dropped passes, eight more than any other team. Against Carolina, Green Bay managed just 66 rushing yards on 26 carries. Opposing defenses continue to make Love beat them through the air. So far, he has. His development into a quarterback capable of carrying an offense is encouraging, and the team’s 5-3 record reflects that resilience. But there’s a difference between having a quarterback who can overcome adversity and building an offense that consistently puts him in that position. The Packers don’t need Love to do more. They need the rest of the offense to do more for him. So what can change? Unfortunately not much! The trade deadline is approaching, and I suppose there’s a possibility that the Packers acquire a new running back. But given the run blocking the team has displayed this year, how much difference might a better back make? Speaking of the line, it’s possible that their run blocking could improve and that could alleviate some of the issues. But don’t hold your breath there. As for pass catchers… anyone can receive a pass, but it’s catching of the pass. That’s the key. Can the Packers receivers turn that around? In the meantime, I’m choosing to simply marvel at the fact that, through 8 games, Jordan Love seems entirely capable of keeping me entertained on Sundays. It’s extremely impressive given the circumstances, and that will have to do. Jordan Love on pace for franchise record Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love leads the NFL in passing yards and is on pace to set the team’s franchise record for single season passing yards through eight weeks of the 2026 season.
