stories.title: Bill Belichick nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame 2027 class after first-ballot snub
stories.summary: Bill Belichick wasn't inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame as part of the class of 2026. He's headed toward the ballot for induction in 2027.
stories.detailText: Bill Belichick is back on the ballot. The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced coach nominees for the Class of 2027 on Nov. 5, with Belichick headlining the list of five. It marks the second consecutive season for the former New England Patriots head coach, who oversaw one of the greatest dynasties in NFL history. Belichick's snub on the first ballot sparked outrage across the football world in January, leaving many to question the Hall of Fame's voting process. Now the path to enshrinement in Canton, Ohio, looks a little different as sweeping changes were enacted in September . The Hall slashed its voting body from 50 members to 25 as part of the change. It will also have three non-voting members that will make up a 28-person selection committee. The three non-voters are set to rotate each season. JARRETT BELL: I'm a Pro Football Hall of Fame voter. We blew it with Bill Belichick snub | Opinion Subcommittees initially debated a list of 14 coaching candidates for enshrinement in 2027 before settling on the list of five that includes Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan. All five nominees found themselves in the same position last year, with Belichick being chosen as the category's representative. And, just like last year, only one will advance out of the group again to be among the 15 finalists that will include 13 modern-era Players, one coach and one contributor. Here's what to know. Why wasn't Bill Belichick inducted into the Hall of Fame? Belichick didn't receive the necessary votes for induction as part of the Class of 2026. Under the previous voting rules, the coach would've needed at least 40 of 50 votes to be enshrined in Aug. 2026. Since voting for the Pro Football Hall of Fame isn't public, it's unclear how many votes Belichick received. Bill Belichick reacts to Hall of Fame snub Belichick spoke about the snub during an interview with Fox News' Sean Hannity on the May 19 episode of the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast . "Well, it's out of my control," Belichick said. "And honestly, I've been very focused on my job at the University of North Carolina and the players and the university there. So, you know, whatever happens, happens. But I'm proud of what we accomplished as teams at New England and certainly at the Giants, and proud of those relationships. So that's what matters most." Belichick said appreciated the outpouring of support for his Hall of Fame case in the immediate aftermath of the 2026 snub. "It’s great to hear that support from so many people and from so many different fields – not just football, but many others," he added. "And so, you know, I was very appreciative of that support and the positive comments that they made." Belichick wasn't willing to speculate on why he wasn't voted in, saying you'd have to ask the voters. Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027 coach nominees Belichick headlines the list of coach nominees for enshrinement as part of the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. The Hall provided a brief bio on each as part of the announcement : Bill Belichick: NFL coach from 1975-2023 with head coaching jobs with the Cleveland Browns (1991-95) and New England Patriots (2000-2023). Career record: 333-178 (including playoffs) with six Super Bowl titles as a head coach and two others as an assistant. Tom Coughlin: Spent 20 years as an NFL head coach with the Jacksonville Jaguars (1995-2002) and New York Giants (2004-2015). Including playoffs, posted a 182-157 record and led the Giants to two Super Bowl titles. Also won a title with Giants as an assistant coach. Mike Holmgren: Head coach of the Green Bay Packers from 1992-98 and the Seattle Seahawks from 1999-2008; won a Super Bowl ring in two Super Bowl trips with the Packers and appeared in another Super Bowl as head coach of the Seahawks. Career record: 174-122 (including postseason). Also won two Super Bowls as an assistant with the San Francisco 49ers. Dan Reeves: Head coach of the Denver Broncos (1981-1992), New York Giants (1993-96) and Atlanta Falcons (1997-2003). Career record: 201-174-2 (including postseason). Led Broncos (three times) and Falcons (once) to the Super Bowl. Won a title as an assistant with the Dallas Cowboys. Mike Shanahan: Head coach of the Los Angeles Raiders (1988-89), Denver Broncos (1995-2008) and Washington Redskins (2010-13). Won back-to-back Super Bowls with the Broncos while compiling a 178-144 career record (including playoffs). Also won a title with the San Francisco 49ers as an assistant coach. Given Belichick's snub last year, it would appear likely that the voting body would avoid a repeat this time around. That would seemingly make the coach a heavy favorite to be inducted. Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027 contributor nominees The Hall announced the list of contributor nominees on Nov. 4, which is headlined by Patriots owner Robert Kraft. Like Belichick, Kraft fell short of receiving the necessary votes for induction in 2026. Here's a look at the full list of nominees, with the bios provided by the Hall : Ralph Hay: Owned the Canton Bulldogs from 1918-1922; hosted the NFL's formational meeting in his automobile dealership in downtown Canton. Robert Kraft: Owner of the New England Patriots since 1994 and chairman and CEO of the Kraft Group. His teams have won six Super Bowls and played in five others – 11 appearances overall in the past 31 seasons. Also key member of several influential NFL owners' committees. Virginia McCaskey: Principal owner of the Chicago Bears from 1983 until her passing in 2025 at age 102. Daughter of team founder George Halas. During her tenure the Bears won Super Bowl XX during a stretch of five consecutive division titles. Doug Williams: Nine-year NFL career was punctuated with a Super Bowl title and game MVP honors following a 340-yard, four-touchdown performance against the Broncos to cap the 1987 season. Has spent the past 13 seasons in the front office of the Commanders’ franchise. Other stints as a scout or front office executive in the NFL came with the Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. John Wooten: An offensive lineman in the NFL for 10 seasons, he transitioned to scouting and player personnel roles with the Cowboys, Eagles and Ravens for nearly three decades. In 2003, became chair of the Fritz Pollard Alliance, a group working to advance opportunities for minorities in coaching and front office positions across pro football. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Bill Belichick nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame 2027 class after first-ballot snub

stories.title: Bears vs. Bucs Injury Report: Monangai DNP, Benedet and Jarrett Upgraded
stories.summary: The Bears’ final injury report for Thursday’s game against the Patriots is out. @ryandroste with the latest.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 08: Jonah Jackson #73 of the Chicago Bears looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at Solider Field on September 8, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois . (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night, and we have both team’s injury report for Thursday’s practices. After conducting a walk-thru on Wednesday, the Bears held a real practice on Thursday which gives us a better window into the team’s status heading into Sunday Night Football. Three players were listed as DNP (did not practice), with two of them being the only real concerns: LB D’Marco Jackson (ankle) and RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe). OL Joe Thuney was listed DNP due to a rest day. Jackson was not listed on the injury report on Wednesday. On the positive side, OL Theo Benedet (shoulder) and DL Grady Jarrett (groin) were both upgraded to “limited” one day after being tagged as DNP. DB Malik Muhammad (toe) was listed as “limited” for the second time this week. #Bears Injury Report pic.twitter.com/NAC7fZoOCS — Bears Communications (@BearsPR) November 5, 2026 Bears RB and Special Teams contributor Zavier Scott was added to injured reserve earlier on Thursday. Monangai continues to be a question mark after missing his fourth game this past Monday night. His availability is once again in question for this weekend, and with the Bears’ bye week following up Sunday night’s game, one has to wonder if the team will hold him out yet again in order to give him a few more weeks to fully heal from his turf toe injury. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers listed the following players as DNP on Thursday: OLB Yaya Diaby (knee), WR Chris Godwin Jr. (rest), RB Bucky Irving (rest), and T Tristan Wirfs (toe). Listed as “limited” by the Bucs were DL A’Shawn Robinson (rest) and S Tykee Smith (ankle). The Bears take on the Bucs Sunday evening at Soldier Field in Chicago, IL. stories.title: Lions, Dolphins Week 9 injury report: Amon-Ra St. Brown limited, Brian Branch full
stories.summary: Taking a closer look at the Lions and Dolphins Thursday injury report for Week 9.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions runs with the ball during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images After holding a walkthrough on Wednesday, the Detroit Lions (5-2) returned to the practice field on Thursday as they prepare to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6). While Wednesday’s report was just estimates from the coaching staff, Thursday’s practice mirrored the same level of participation for most players, with a couple of upgrades. With that in mind, here’s Thursday’s injury report and what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Estimated n o practice C Cade Mays (ankle) — Preparing for Juice Scruggs to start EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion) LB Jack Campbell (neck) CB D.J. Reed (hip) Earlier in the week, coach Dan Campbell suggested Mays might miss Wednesday and Thursday’s practices, so this isn’t a surprise, but it’s still unclear whether he can return on Friday. Campbell said the team is preparing to start Scruggs this week, but nothing is finalized. Wonnum is still in the NFL’s concussion protocol, and while he still has a chance to pass the protocols this week, his lack of return to practice suggests he is a bit further back than hoped. No updates on Campbell since Wednesday . Reed said he was in a good spot in his post-game media availability last Sunday, so his absence from practice could mean his injury was worse than he realized or that the team is giving the veteran extra time to be ready. We’ll find out more on Friday. Estimated limited practice RB Jacob Saylors (neck) WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 12 Saylors popped up on last week’s injury report with a neck injury and was also forced from the game because of it, but getting in practice reps is a good sign he’s headed in the right direction. St. Brown got a little banged up in Week 7, but it’s rare to see him scale back even a little, so it’s not surprising that he was back on the practice field this week, and expectations are that he is on track to play against the Dolphins. Joseph is expanding his practice exposure this week, but the team is not going to rush him back, and Campbell has already said they don’t plan to activate him this week. He still has 12 days left in his injury evaluation window, which could put him in play for the Lions-Patriots game in Germany, or potentially the following week when they host the Bucs. Estimated full practice LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (toe) CB Rock Ya-Sin (cramps) S Brian Branch (concussion) Ogbongbemiga did not appear to suffer an injury in Week 7, but he showed up on this week’s injury report with a toe injury. Not much is known about this injury, but getting in a full practice is a good sign he may be able to play on Sunday. If not, the Lions did add two linebackers to the active roster this week and another to the practice squad, in case the team needs more depth. Ya-Sin was added to the injury report with “cramps,” suggesting he required fluids, but there shouldn’t be too much to worry about long term as long as he manages his hydration. Branch is making steady progress through the NFL’s concussion protocols and was on the practice field on Thursday, suggesting he is positioning himself to play on Sunday. He still has steps to clear, including clearance from an independent doctor, but things look on track for now. Dolphin s’ injury report Coming soon.

stories.title: Patriots re-sign veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor to practice squad
stories.summary: Kindle Vildor had been released from the 53-man roster earlier in the week.
stories.detailText: Oct 11, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots cornerback Kindle Vildor (28) looks on against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second quarter at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A veteran of 85 NFL games has returned to Gillette Stadium to fill the open spot on the practice squad. The New England Patriots officially re-signed cornerback Kindle Vildor to the 17-man scout team on Thursday after he had been released from the 53-man roster earlier in the week. Vildor, 28, first made his way to Foxborough on a one-year contract as an unrestricted free agent in March. The 5-foot-11, 190-pound vested corner intercepted a pass in preseason action before beginning the regular season on the practice squad. After serving as a standard elevation for the 29-26 AFC East upset of the Buffalo Bills, he was promoted to the active roster and earned a game ball from head coach Mike Vrabel following the 45-17 rout of the Las Vegas Raiders. In all, Vildor has appeared in five games this fall while notching seven tackles, including one for loss, as well as one forced fumble and one pass deflection. His stay spans 53 snaps on defense to go with 32 snaps on special teams. New England currently carries Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III, Marcus Jones, Charles Woods, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty on the active cornerback depth chart, while the midweek re-signing joins Al’zillion Hamilton on the practice squad. Entering the NFL with the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, Vildor has also made stops with Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. A 27-game starter during his time in the league, the Georgia Southern product has recorded 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions through 2,158 snaps on defense and 605 snaps on special teams. After safety Elliott Davison cleared waivers and circled back, one spot remained vacant on the practice squad. The Green Bay Packers visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

While the Seahawks listed Lock as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report, he said his elbow is doing "a lot better." " It’s doing good, doing good ," Lock said in his Thursday press conference. "I’m excited to be back out there. It felt great to get under center and rip some balls yesterday. So, it feels good." Robinson leads the NFL in rushing yards and he's fourth in yards from scrimmage, but he said on Thursday that he feels like those numbers are not telling the full story of how he is doing on the field this season. stories.title: Mike Holmgren again among nominees for Pro Football Hall of Fame
stories.summary: The Seahawks franchise legend has made it to the final selection process twice before.
stories.detailText: DETROIT, MI - FEBRUARY 5: Mike Holmgren head coach of the Seattle Seahawks during Super Bowl XL played between the Pittsburgh Steelers and The Seattle Seahawks at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. The Steelers defeated the Seahawks by a score of 21 to 10. (Photo by Rob Tringali/SportsChrome/Getty Images) | Getty Images A franchise legend could be Canton bound. The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced the five final coach nominees for the Class of 2027 on Thursday, and among the quintet is former Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Holmgren. Joining Holmgren to round out the finalists is Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Dan Reeves, and Mike Shanahan. The Coach Subcommittee has narrowed its list to five nominees for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. https://t.co/470uoLXcHX pic.twitter.com/pJ8d3b5lN8 — Pro Football Hall of Fame (@ProFootballHOF) November 5, 2026 In the new Hall of Fame selection process, only one of the five coach nominees will be selected to advance to the full selection committee, which will cast its ballots in the new year. Holmgren has twice made it to the full selection committee, in 2020 and 2025, but was not elected either time . Last year, Belichick infamously made it to the selection committee only to be denied. Holmgren coached the Seahawks for 10 seasons, leading the franchise to its first Super Bowl appearance, a 21-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XL. He also went to two Super Bowls with the Green Bay Packers, winning Super Bowl 31 before losing Super Bowl 32. Seattle won the division five times during his tenure and made six playoff appearances. He retired as the franchise’s all-time leader in coaching wins and was inducted into the team’s Ring of Honor in 2021. On Monday night, Holmgren raised the 12 flag before Seattle’s game against the Chicago Bears. Mike Holmgren raised the 12 Flag for our Monday Night Football game! pic.twitter.com/1r8uJHcAPi — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 3, 2026

stories.title: Vikings to start QB Carson Wentz against Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out
stories.summary: Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out with a hamstring injury.
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings have once again hopped on their quarterback carousel. Backup Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills , coach Kevin O'Connell announced Thursday, because starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring. The change marks the 14th time the Vikings have shifted from one quarterback to another during a season, either because of injuries or for performance reasons, since Kirk Cousins tore his right Achilles tendon midway through the 2023 season. Murray suffered the injury while running on a read-option play early in the fourth quarter of the Vikings' 19-15 loss last Sunday to the Detroit Lions . Murray also struggled to connect with open receivers throughout the game, leaving receiver Justin Jefferson so frustrated that he declined to speak with reporters afterward. O'Connell said that putting Murray on injured reserve is not a consideration. "I don't believe it to be much more than a week-to-week kind of thing right now," O'Connell said. "But for him, his movement skills and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we'd be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on." Murray scrambled seven times during a Week 4 game against the New Orleans Saints but has run only 13 times in his five remaining starts. But O'Connell said the injury would affect more than simply his ability to run. "It's more the explosive movements, the quick-twitch movements," O'Connell said. "Running is obviously a part of some of that ... but it's more of just the overall ability to impact the game. And ultimately, we could try to say all we want of, 'Hey, you can play, but you just got to stay in the pocket.' But then football starts, and it's an imperfect game where he's going to react and we don't want to make this strain any worse than it is." Murray missed most of two games earlier this season because of a concussion, and his QBR (44.7) ranks No. 26 out of 30 qualified quarterbacks as he plays on a one-year contract. Speaking Monday, O'Connell said that Murray would remain his starter this week if he were healthy. Asked Thursday if Wentz had an opportunity to earn additional starts based on his performance, independent of Murray's health, O'Connell said in part: "It's all about this week for our team." Wentz has started six games and played most of a seventh since signing with the Vikings in August 2025. The team is 4-3 in those games, during which Wentz has completed 63.9% of his passes for 1,492 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. He has excelled in getting the ball to Jefferson, however. In those seven games, Jefferson has caught 44 passes for 615 yards and two touchdowns. "[Wentz] is the perfect guy in a moment where you can't have Kyler out there at full strength to go in there," O'Connell said. "And we feel very strongly about when Carson's in there, we're going to get really effective quarterback play."

stories.title: Irving and the Buccaneers visit Swift and the Bears in a matchup of the NFL's top rushing teams
stories.summary: — Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson knows a little something about a successful rushing attack. And he's impressed with Tampa Bay's ground game.
stories.detailText: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson knows a little something about a successful rushing attack. And he's impressed with Tampa Bay's ground game. The NFL's top rushing teams face off when Bucky Irving and Tampa Bay visit D’Andre Swift and Chicago on Sunday night. The Buccaneers are averaging a league-high 168.6 yards on the ground, and the Bears are second at 150.8 yards per game. “I mean, I’m telling you, this offensive line is really good,” Johnson said. “The scheme is really good. They have a lot of variety with which they do things. Then the backs are phenomenal as well. It’s a potent, potent rushing attack. ... So that’ll be a huge challenge for us.” Tampa Bay's ground game was so good in Week 8 that it beat Atlanta 16-0 without completing a pass. Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown in wet conditions as the Buccaneers set a franchise record with 324 yards on the ground. Tampa Bay is averaging 231.3 yards rushing over its past four games, winning three times during the impressive stretch. “I think we’ve tweaked some things, obviously, in how we’re running it and the things that certain guys can do well up front, as well as what kind of runs the backs can do," coach Todd Bowles said. “I think the coaches get more comfortable with the players and vice versa, and everybody is settling into the scheme and kind of buying in and being on the same page, really.” Tampa Bay's tight ends — especially Cade Otton and Payne Durham — have played an important role in clearing the way for Irving and Kenny Gainwell , who rushed for 140 yards against the Falcons. “The last couple of weeks we’re riding the hot hand with the run game, and it’s been great with the 12, 13 personnel and the heavier sets,” quarterback Baker Mayfield said. Chicago's ground game has slowed since a fast start. The Bears rushed for 785 yards in their first four games, averaging 4.9 yards per carry, and 421 in their past four, averaging 3.5 yards per attempt. Swift scored three touchdowns during Monday night’s 34-17 win at Seattle, but he finished with just 69 yards on a season-high 27 carries. Fellow running back Kyle Monangai could return against the Bucs after missing four games with thumb and toe injuries. “It’s been a little bit spotty. We stick with it though,” Johnson said. “I know first-half rushing hasn’t been as effective as second-half rushing. That’s one of those things that I know that eventually we will break through. We’re too good up front not to do that.” Need to know Tampa Bay (3-5) at Chicago (6-2) When/where to watch: Sunday 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC. Latest odds: Bears by 6 1/2. Against the spread: Buccaneers 3-5, Bears 6-2. Last week: Buccaneers beat the Falcons 16-0; Bears beat the Seahawks 34-17. Last meeting: Buccaneers beat the Bears 27-17 on Sept. 17, 2023. Series record: Bears lead 40-22. Matchup to watch Buccaneers NT Vita Vea vs. Bears C Garrett Bradbury . The 31-year-old Vea is one of the NFL's top interior defensive linemen. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 347 pounds, he helped the Bucs limit the Falcons to 99 yards rushing and 224 yards overall. Vea agreed to a contract extension in August. Bradbury took over at center for Chicago after he was acquired in an offseason trade with New England. He has started each of his 113 career games. Stats and stuff — It's the first meeting between Mayfield, the No. 1 pick in the 2018 draft, and Bears quarterback Caleb Williams , the top selection in 2024. Mayfield is 13-11 when facing a No. 1 overall pick as the opponent’s starting QB, including an 8-6 record in such games with Tampa Bay. — Chicago leads the NFL with 3,098 yards on offense. The Bears have the No. 3 total offense in the league, averaging 387.3 yards per game. — Tampa Bay cornerback Zyon McCollum is going for his third consecutive game with an interception. — Irving is from Chicago and played for Hillcrest High School, about 25 miles south of Soldier Field. — Swift has rushed for seven TDs in the past four games and a career-high 10 on the season. He has 48 rushing touchdowns in 97 career games. — The Bears have an NFL-high 22 drives of five-plus minutes this season. They also lead the league in average time of possession at 35:27. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: A 49ers trade deadline wishlist: 7 players who could help win a Super Bowl
stories.summary: We looked at several players who could make the 49ers a better team heading into the second half
stories.detailText: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers find themselves in a unique spot entering Week 9. Despite having plenty of needs (pass rusher, secondary, and receiver, to name a few), the 49ers are sitting pretty at 6-1 with a three-game advantage in the loss column in the NFC West. San Francisco has already made a splash and cleaned up a need by bringing in another old friend in DeForest Buckner, but it can’t hurt the 49ers to make at least another move or two. So here’s my wishlist. Some bigger asks than others, but all within different realms of possibility. If the 49ers can acquire one of the below names, I’ll be happy. Two, I’d be ecstatic. And three or more, I will be thinking about the route for the Super Bowl parade. With the trade deadline right around the corner, here’s my list of the players the 49ers should be looking at: WR Garrett Wilson, Jets Wilson would be that high-end item you put on a wishlist that you know is too pricey to ask for, but you ask for it just in case. It would be hard to imagine the 49ers acquiring a better player at any position (let alone a position of need). The 49ers need a receiver, even with a few coming back from injury over the next few weeks, and Wilson would be the perfect complement across from Mike Evans. Wilson started his career with three consecutive 1,000-yard seasons with Zach Wilson, Mike White, Joe Flacco, Trevor Siemian, and Aaron Rodgers throwing passes to him. Now with Geno Smith as his quarterback, Wilson has 527 yards, pacing for another 1,000-yard season. You can’t blame 49ers fans for imagining what Wilson could be with Purdy as his quarterback. If the price is too high on Wilson, John Lynch and Co. would be smart to inquire about Adonai Mitchell before hanging up on the Jets. S Jessie Bates III, Falcons Your guess is as good as mine if Bates will even be available. Some weeks, Atlanta is good enough to beat a 6-0 49ers team, but others they’re bad enough to lose to a team that doesn’t complete a pass. With the state of the NFC South, you can’t blame the Falcons if they choose to stand pat, but if they are taking calls, Bates would be an ideal trade target for San Francisco. The 49ers have flirted with the idea of Bates, both when he was available for trade when he played for the Bengals and when he was a free agent before he signed with Atlanta. The safety play for the 49ers has been inconsistent this season, and Bates would add stability. Plus there’s already a connection there with Bates playing under 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris in 2023 and 2024, earning a second-team All-Pro nod in the latter year. Bates would be pricey and might need an extension to make a deal work, but he could be a long-term fix to one of the 49ers’ shakier position groups. WR Josh Downs, Colts The Santa Clara-Indianapolis pipeline has already been tapped once with the Buckner trade, so negotiations will be familiar waters for Lynch if he wants to return to that well. If the Jets hold onto Wilson or the 49ers miss out, Downs wouldn’t be a bad consolation. Per NFL Next Gen stats, Downs is a better separator than Wilson, averaging 3.0 yards of separation per route run compared to Wilson’s 2.6. Downs has used that ability to separate to lead the Colts in targets (51), receiving yards (330), and first downs (19). Downs would have a lower cost to acquire than Wilson (although Wilson would be a long-term fix and future replacement for Mike Evans) and would be a clear No. 2 in an injured but crowded wide receiver room. If I had to pick the likeliest player acquired by the 49ers before the trade deadline, I would wager on Downs. DE Josh Sweat, Cardinals An inter-division trade feels unlikely, and the Cardinals can drive the price as high as they want with two more years of control of Sweat, but if the 49ers want to make a huge swing for the fences, Sweat would be the guy. Sweat’s 40.5 sacks career total ranks 12th among all defenders (with only a sack more than Nick Bosa), with 12 sacks in 2025 after signing a four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Cardinals. He hasn’t quite had that success yet this season, recording just three sacks in eight games so far this season. But while his production has been down in 2026, Sweat gives something the 49ers don’t see too often in their pass rushers: a clean bill of health. Sweat has missed only three games since 2021 and hasn’t missed a game since signing with Arizona. The price would be high, but Sweat would be a true 1B to Bosa’s 1A, and if a trade for the Arizona pass rusher is the catalyst for the 49ers’ pass rush becoming elite again, how high is too high? DE Khalil Mack, Chargers A more logical choice would be Mack, but the Chargers don’t seem convinced that an 0-7 start in the AFC West is an impossible task to overcome. If Los Angeles comes to its senses and starts selling, the 49ers should be all over the veteran end. The 49ers have been tied to Mack since he donned the Silver and Black, but the two sides have narrowly missed several times. San Francisco was also interested in Mack when he hit free agency after his time with Chicago,hicago but he went to Los Angeles instead. Maybe the third time will be the charm. Mack isn’t the elite defender he was once, but his 5.5 sacks in 2025 would have led to the 49ers, and his three sacks would be only behind Keion White this season. But unlike in Los An,geles where Mack is the No. 1 pass rusher, he’d be behind Bosa and would draw more favorable matchups than he’s currently facing. San Francisco has flirted with Mack a few times already; maybe the match is finally made before Tuesday’s deadline. DE Jadeveon Clowney, Texans The 49ers have had a need for a second pass rusher for as long as Bosa has been with the franchise. Clowney has been on seven different teams over his 13-year career and four teams over the last four seasons. Somehow, the two have never come together. The Texans enter Week 9 with a 2-5 record, and with Clowney on a one-year deal, there’s no reason to think the veteran can’t be had for cheap. And Clowney has shown he can still go, even on the wrong side of 30. Clowney, at age 33, ranks 12th of all active players with 25.5 sacks after turning 30 , but ranks behind only TJ Watt and Danielle Hunter on the list as the only players in their age-33 season or younger. Clowney to San Francisco has made almost too much sense for too long, and if San Francisco doesn’t land Sweat or Mack, Clowney would absolutely work. WR Chimere Dike, Titans Allow me to pull one completely out of left field. But let’s say the 49ers’ plan to get better at receiver is to wait for the returns of Demarcus Robinson (which feels sooner rather than later) and De’Zhaun Stribling (which feels later rather than sooner). Or let’s say the 49ers even try to rebuild a bridge with a certain player who is reportedly showing up to work on Friday. Let’s just call it a choose-your-own-adventure to why the 49ers opt not to go after Wilson, Mitchell, or Downs. But maybe they remember what Rashid Shaheed not only did for the Seahawks last season, but what Shaheed did to the 49ers in the playoffs. So what if, instead of going for the big fish at receiver, they instead use the position to solve the long-standing returner issue? The Titans would have no motivation to move Dike with him only in his second season, but with Jeffrey Simmons already gone, it would cause no harm for the 49ers to at least call. If San Francisco does pull the trigger, Dike would become one of the best returners in 49ers history on day one if he continues his pace he’s shown in Tennessee. Dike has 94 kickoff returns so far in his season and a half with the Titans. Only five players in 49ers history (Super Bowl era) have taken more than 75 kickoff returns (Vic Washington, Ted Ginn, Maurice Hicks, Carl Monroe, and Dexter Carter), and Dike’s 25.7 yards per those 94 returns would rank second behind only Washington. The same would apply for punt returns as well. Dike has 34 of those to his name, and while plenty of 49ers (Super Bowl era) have taken at least 30 punt returns (23 to be exact), none are better than Dike’s 15.7 yards per punt return. Dike could add something to the receiver room (59 receptions for 579 yards on 88 targets), but man, wouldn’t it be nice to have a good returner one time in Santa Clara.

stories.title: Should Ravens move on from Lamar Jackson after 2026? The case for and against it
stories.summary: Is Lamar Jackson out for the season? The answer may affect what the QB's future looks like with the Baltimore Ravens.
stories.detailText: How the Baltimore Ravens answer the question of Lamar Jackson's future in Charm City can and will shape the franchise over the next five to 10 years. To paraphrase The Clash: should he stay or should he go? On its face, the thought of the Ravens parting with Jackson – a two-time MVP, second-winningest quarterback in franchise history, No. 2 all-time rusher and passer for the franchise – seems ludicrous. Looking around the league at other teams stuck in quarterback purgatory, why would Baltimore choose to subject itself to an uncertain future? To answer a question with a question: do the Ravens want to pay their star quarterback a base salary of more than $50 million in 2027, with the knowledge of his unlucky history with injuries and that he could walk away in 2028? LAMAR JACKSON: Is Ravens QB out for the season? Latest injury update Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta and head coach Jesse Minter face a major decision heading into this offseason. Should they get it wrong, the rest of the 2020s might be real rough for the Ravens. Here's a closer look at Jackson's contract details as he misses more time in the penultimate year of his current deal, as well as arguments for why the team should or should not stick with him: Lamar Jackson contract details Term: Five years Total value: $260 million Average annual value (AAV): $52 million Guaranteed money: $185 million Jackson is in the fourth year of the five-year extension he signed with the Ravens in 2023. The veteran quarterback is due to hit free agency after 2027, but his deal also includes three void years in 2028, 2029 and 2030. As a result, there will be a $42.5 million dead cap hit that accelerates onto Baltimore's books in 2028, barring a further extension. The biggest other note about Jackson's contract is that his 2027 cap hit is projected to be larger than the dead cap the Ravens would have to eat in a trade or (unlikely) release. The quarterback's deal is responsible for either an $84.3 million cap hit next year or $74.8 million in dead cap. Assuming the Ravens choose to keep Jackson in Baltimore next year, another contract restructure to lighten the load of the cap hit would be all but certain. If the team does want to move on from the quarterback, a post-June 1 trade (or release) would be the likely result. The post-June 1 designation would spread out the dead cap hit into more manageable hits: $32.3 million in 2027 and then $42.5 million total (including accelerated void years) in 2028, per Over The Cap . Why the Ravens should part with Lamar Jackson Two main reasons here: injuries and money. Jackson's latest injury – of the thumb variety and "potentially" season-ending, according to Minter – is already his second this season and the sixth significant injury of his career. With the thumb injury due to land Jackson on injured reserve, he's guaranteed to miss at least four games in a season for the fourth time in the last six seasons. The impact of those injuries on the Ravens is significant. This year, they're 3-1 with Jackson and 1-3 without him (we're counting Week 8 as "without him" since he played exactly one snap). Prior to this year, the team went 1-4 without Jackson in 2021, 2-3 without him in 2022 and 2-2 with Jackson missing in 2025. Baltimore missed the playoffs by one game in 2021 and 2025. In 2022, they narrowly made the postseason thanks to an 8-4 start under Jackson, but the Ravens lost immediately in the wild-card round without him. Baltimore might want to move on from a quarterback whose durability is coming into question – especially given how much they're set to pay him next year. Jackson is due more than $51 million in base salary next year, and his contract will carry a cap hit of $84.3 million in 2027. As things stand, that would be the largest cap hit for a single player in history – by a wide margin. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys hold the record with his $50.5 million hit last year. The Ravens have a way out of Jackson's big-money extension after this year. A pre-June 1 trade or release would result in a $74.8 million cap hit. That's an unlikely solution, but it would save the team more than $9.5 million in cap space. A more likely solution would be a post-June 1 cut or trade. Such a move would save the Ravens $52 million in cap space in 2027. And trading Jackson could be particularly enticing for the Ravens. The quarterback's contract includes a provision that states the team cannot designate him with a franchise or transition tag (again) once the deal expires after the 2027 season. That means Baltimore doesn't have much of a safety net if it fails to reach an extension with Jackson, who represents himself, and he could walk in free agency in 2028 with no return for the team. A trade would allow the Ravens to get a huge haul of picks for Jackson and set up their future. They'd undoubtedly receive multiple first-round picks and more for the two-time MVP, who won't turn 30 until January. Why the Ravens should not part with Lamar Jackson Seriously? Besides the injuries and cap hit, pretty much every single other reason. Off the bat, here's an easy answer to their cap woes: they could sign the quarterback to an extension that will help relieve the $84.3 million hit the team is set to take on next year. Jackson didn't want to engage in negotiations before the 2026 season, but with him due to miss significant time and enter a walk year with no deal in place, signs point to a more willing negotiator. Let's say that cap situation doesn't get solved quickly and easily. There are still plenty of reasons to hold onto Jackson. First, let's focus on the 31 other teams that aren't the Ravens. How many have no clear future at quarterback heading into 2027? How many teams that believe they have a franchise quarterback still wish they had Jackson leading their offense instead? Baltimore has the luxury of already knowing they got it right at quarterback. When Jackson is healthy and playing well – as he was for three and a half games to start the year – he's an incredible talent as a rusher and as a passer. His ceiling, we already know, is unanimous MVP winner. In eight-plus years in the league, Jackson is 18 wins away from surpassing Joe Flacco to become the Ravens' all-time wins leader. He's also second in franchise history with 23,575 passing yards and 193 passing touchdowns. His 102.7 passer rating is the best in Ravens history, as are his 7.9 yards per attempt. That's only as a passer. Jackson is also a game-breaker with his legs. He ranks second in Ravens history with 6,666 rushing yards and fourth with 36 career rushing touchdowns. The quarterback's 6.1 yards per rush attempt are second-most of any Raven with at least 100 rush attempts (he has 1,100), and his 55.1 rush yards per game rank ninth all-time for the franchise. Here are a few more quick-hitting insights into Jackson's impact from just this year, courtesy of USA TODAY Sports' Nate Davis : Baltimore has 14 touchdowns in the 14 quarters Jackson has played this year, discounting Sunday. The Ravens have six TDs in the 19 quarters without him. Running back Derrick Henry averaged 104.5 yards from scrimmage in the season’s first four games – mostly with Jackson – and scored seven TDs. Since? It’s been 72.3 yards per game and two end-zone trips. The last playoff game the franchise won without Jackson was at the end of the 2014 season, nearly three years before he was drafted. Giving up Jackson to pursue another quarterback in a trade invites unnecessary uncertainty into Baltimore's future. Sure, the next quarterback could turn out to be anything – even the next Lamar Jackson – but why risk it? The free-agent quarterback class is headlined by Deshaun Watson, Aaron Rodgers (who says he's retiring), Kyler Murray and (with his likely release) Kirk Cousins. Baltimore could roll the dice on Anthony Richardson if he hits the open market, or rely on Mac Jones having a Sam Darnold-like renaissance after spending time with Kyle Shanahan, but those are risks. Then there's the draft, which features a quarterback class that looks weaker every week of the college football season that passes. Maybe the Ravens hit on finding a franchise QB in the draft for a third time in a row. But why invite that risk with Jackson – a two-time MVP looking like he could have competed for a third this year before his injury – already in-house? USA TODAY Sports' Nate Davis contributed. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Should Ravens move on from Lamar Jackson after 2026? The case for and against it

stories.title: Cowboys offensive line vs. Colts defensive line examined
stories.summary: How do you feel about the Cowboys offensive line this week?
stories.detailText: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images If the Cowboys want to get back on the winning track, a dominant performance from their offensive line would certainly help. Let’s see how they match up against the Colts defensive line. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 53% (8th) Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st) Pressure rate allowed – 30% (15th) Sacks allowed – 11 (4th) Last three-week trend: One step forward, one step back The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Adetomiwa Adebawore is now the player Dallas has to find DeForest Buckner is gone after Indianapolis traded the three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle to San Francisco last week. That sounds like great news for Dallas, but his replacement might actually be the most dangerous individual pass-rushing matchup on the Colts defense. Adetomiwa Adebawore has quietly put together an excellent season. PFF currently credits him with 16 pressures and five sacks, while his 84.4 pass-rush grade ranks third among qualifying interior defensive linemen. That is the matchup Dallas cannot overlook simply because Buckner has left town. Interior pressure is especially dangerous for Prescott. When an edge defender gets around Tyler Guyton or Terence Steele, Dak Prescott can often step forward. When Adebawore wins directly through the middle, there is nowhere to step. That puts Tyler Smith, Cooper Beebe and Tyler Booker under pressure to restore order after a poor performance against Arizona. PRESSURE POINT: The tackles need a response Tyler Guyton had been enjoying a strong season before Sunday, then Arizona changed that. Guyton finished with a 44.7 PFF grade, while Terence Steele was only slightly better at 48.2. Four of Dallas’ five starting offensive linemen graded below 50. Indianapolis does not have an elite edge rush, but there are still players capable of punishing another poor performance. Laiatu Latu earned an 84.0 PFF grade against Jacksonville and recorded a sack. Jaylahn Tuimoloau also recorded a sack and generated four pressures, producing a 22.2% pressure win rate in the game. Still, the Colts rank last in ESPN Pass Rush Win Rate. If Guyton and Steele surrender quick pressure anyway, it becomes a major concern for a Cowboys offensive line that was supposed to be settling down. Against Philadelphia, Prescott was barely touched. Against Arizona, he went down four times. Dallas needs the Philadelphia version back. WHERE TO ATTACK Every defensive line has a weakness, here’s the Colts soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run straight at the post-Buckner Colts This might be the clearest green light Dallas has seen all season. Indianapolis has allowed: 1,054 rushing yards 131.8 rushing yards per game 4.9 yards per carry 26% Run Stop Win Rate which ranks 29th Then the Colts traded Buckner. Their first game without him ended with Jacksonville rushing for 183 yards, that is an invitation. Dallas cannot respond by putting everything back on Prescott. Javonte Williams carried 24 times against Arizona but gained only 56 yards. The blocking simply did not give him anywhere to go so this week needs to look different. Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker are two powerful guards. Cooper Beebe can work combination blocks with either of them. Dallas should use that interior strength and force Indianapolis to prove it can hold up without Buckner. Even Grover Stewart has not been dominant this season. His current PFF run-defense grade sits at 60.4, 43rd among qualifying interior defenders. Adebawore has been much more dangerous rushing the passer than anchoring an entire run defense, so make them both play the run and make Indianapolis’ linebackers tackle Williams repeatedly. And most importantly, do not abandon the run if the first few attempts only gain three yards. The Colts have been worn down by opposing running games all season. Dallas should test that weakness for four quarters. GREEN LIGHT: Make Indianapolis win with its four-man pass rush The ESPN number is difficult to ignore as you will see below, Indianapolis’ Pass Rush Win Rate is at 40%, that ranks 32nd. That means the Colts have been the NFL’s least successful team at quickly defeating pass blocks on an individual basis, and their sack production confirms it. Indianapolis has only 16 sacks through eight games, that ranks 23rd. Dallas should trust its offensive line when the Colts send four. Put the running backs and tight ends into routes and force Indianapolis to cover CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson and the running backs. If Indianapolis wants to rush four, Dallas’ five offensive linemen need to win. The Chaos Report Here’s the Arizona Cardinals defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 16 (23rd) Pass Rush Win Rate – 40% (32nd) Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (28th) QB Pressure Rate – 21% (32nd) Last three-week trend: Weak and getting weaker Matchup of the week Tyler Smith vs. Adetomiwa Adebawore When Indianapolis lines Adebawore up across from Tyler Smith, watch it, this is strength against strength. Adebawore is now the most disruptive interior pass rusher on the Colts roster and Smith is the Cowboys offensive lineman best equipped to deal with that combination of speed and power. Adebawore is only 282 pounds, which makes this matchup particularly interesting. He wins with explosion and quickness, and Smith wins with strength. When the Cowboys run, Smith needs to put his hands on Adebawore early and move him, instead of allowing him to shoot through a gap. That also helps later in pass protection. If Adebawore spends the afternoon dealing with Smith coming forward in the running game, he cannot simply spend every snap attacking backwards toward Prescott. Best Route to Success Dallas should not make this game complicated since the Colts cannot stop the run and those numbers should immediately tell Brian Schottenheimer where this game needs to begin. Get Smith and Booker moving forward, feed Williams, use play-action once Indianapolis starts bringing its linebackers downhill, then trust the tackles against a pass rush that ranks last in Pass Rush Win Rate. Dallas cannot repeat what happened against Arizona, where one week of dominant offensive-line play disappeared immediately. The Cowboys have already shown how good this unit can look, Indianapolis provides the perfect opportunity to prove Philadelphia was not a fluke. Injury Updates: Dallas currently has no new injury concerns among its five starting offensive linemen, but keep watch on Jake Ferguson. This could bring Brevyn Spann-Ford to the mix who’s been a much better blocker this year. Veteran edge defender Arden Key remains on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, while Micheal Clemons has also been on IR with a toe injury.

stories.title: Bill Belichick, snubbed from Pro Football Hall of Fame last year, among 5 coach nominees advancing in candidacy for 2027 class
stories.summary: Belichick's exclusion from the 2026 class drew ire throughout the football world.
stories.detailText: Bill Belichick guided the New England Patriots to six Super Bowl victories during his dynastic run as the franchise's head coach. (Photo by Simon Bruty/Anychance/Getty Images) Simon M Bruty via Getty Images The Pro Football Hall of Fame voting process came under fire and was thrust under a microscope last winter when Bill Belichick, arguably the greatest coach in NFL history, was denied first-ballot status . Almost a year later, the Hall is moving forward in its annual consideration of potential new inductees. Belichick is once again up for enshrinement. He's among five former NFL head coaches — the others being Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan — who have advanced in their candidacy to be elected into the 2027 class, the Hall announced Thursday . Five former head coaches - Bill Belichick, Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan - have advanced in the process for possible election to the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2027. pic.twitter.com/RAcJYT0I3e — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 5, 2026 Members from the coach subcommittee whittled down a list that originally included 14 nominees. Next, the subcommittee will thoroughly review the five remaining coaches in contention on Nov. 17, when it meets virtually to pick one of them to present to the full selection committee. Belichick, Coughlin, Holmgren, Reeves and Shanahan all reached this stage of the selection process last year. Ultimately, Belichick — best known for leading the New England Patriots to six Super Bowl victories during his dynastic run as the franchise's head coach — was picked as the candidate from that category to be up for election. Keep in mind, of a class' 15 finalists presented at the selection committee's annual meeting, only one coach and one "contributor" are included. The other 13 nominees are modern-era players. A coach hasn't been enshrined into the Hall since former Cardinals and Chargers frontman Don Coryell went in posthumously as part of the 2023 class. To be enshrined, a candidate must receive at least 80% approval from the member selection committee. Previously, that usually meant a candidate needed 40 votes. Since, however, the board of selectors has shrunk to 28, and just 25 of them will actually vote . Even though Belichick was the subcommittee's pick to be in the running for induction last year, he still had to meet that 80% threshold while competing with a contributor — ironically, Patriots owner Robert Kraft — and three "seniors" — Kenny Anderson, Roger Craig and L.C. Greenwood — in a separate part of the ballot. A minimum of one person and a maximum of three from those combined categories could be elected, per then-existing Hall bylaws. Through all of that complicated mess, Belichick fell short of the necessary votes , leading to ubiquitous outrage, with countless people vouching for Belichick, including his longtime quarterback, Tom Brady, and even Kraft . Craig wound up emerging from the group of nominees that featured Belichick last year . The iconic San Francisco 49ers running back eventually gave a touching pre-recorded speech upon his induction, during which he divulged that he has vascular dementia. Back in September, significant changes were announced to the Hall's selection process. One of those was the elimination of the "seniors" category (every player will now be considered in the same pool). Another was the reduction of the selection committee, effectively from 50 to 25 members (there are three alternates in the current system). Under the Hall's latest bylaws, an induction class can consist of between three and seven honorees. It still takes 80% approval for enshrinement. Also notable, the Hall decided its selection committee will return to discussing and submitting their final votes in person . That dialogue, in conjunction with the final voting process, had been held virtually since the COVID-19 pandemic, as reported by The Associated Press . In early 2027, the selection committee will cast ballots to determine who earns spots in the upcoming class. On Wednesday, the Hall announced that Kraft is one of the five contributors who have advanced in their candidacy to be elected into the 2027 class. The class will be announced at "NFL Honors" in Los Angeles in February ahead of Super Bowl LXI, then enshrined in August in Canton, Ohio.

stories.title: Browns' Jared Verse says he's spoken to teammates about not defending him after getting body-slammed by Steelers' Mason McCormick
stories.summary: McCormick was penalized for unnecessary roughness on the play.
stories.detailText: Jared Verse said Thursday that he has spoken with his Cleveland Browns teammates about not coming to his defense after Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick slammed him to the ground following a point-after attempt on Sunday. "That's a conversation that we've had and spoken about," Verse said . "I've made my issues known about the situation, but also I didn't put them in a position to let them know beforehand I was going to talk the way I talked to the Steelers and Steelers Nation or whatever they are. I got to be better than that. I didn't do enough on my part. We all got to pick it up." McCormick received a 15-yard penalty after he caught a leaping Verse in the air and dumped him to the ground during the Steelers' 27-6 win . He said afterward he didn't know who the player was that he was tangled up with. Mason McCormick with the body slam on the Browns! #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/M0L2gRyqFU — Blitzburgh (@Blitz_Burgh) November 1, 2026 "Just felt somebody jump, and we're told to get jumpers' hands down, and that's really it," McCormick said. "To be quite honest with you, that was the play that made me really angry," Verse said. "I was already upset about the game, the way things were moving, but at that point it became really deep. You're doing dirty s***, you're trying to sweep my legs out. That honestly could have put me in a position to not be able to finish the season, put me in a position to change my life in a very bad aspect, so that upset me. "The lack of reaction by those around me had upset me a lot. They were focused on the game and everything like that, but a similar play happened to Derek Barnett on the next field goal, and I lost it. Because those are my brothers, those are my teammates, and when you do something like that to them, it upsets me very deeply. … These are my teammates, these are my brothers, and we're not fighting for each other." There was tension entering the game between Verse and the Steelers after the Browns defensive end called out Pittsburgh for playing "dirty" when the two last met in Week 4. He also said Cleveland was going to "make Pittsburgh ours" in the days leading up to their Week 9 matchup. "I'm very upset about it and if this wasn't football I'd be acting a different way," Verse said after the game about the play adding, "To do something like that, I just can't have respect for that."

stories.title: CB DJ Turner upgraded to full practice for Bengals
stories.summary: Cornerback DJ Turner's status took a step in a positive direction on the Bengals' Thursday practice report.
stories.detailText: Cornerback DJ Turner's status took a step in a positive direction on the Bengals' Thursday practice report. Turner was listed as a full participant in practice. He was listed as out of practice on Wednesday due to a heel issue, but that upgrade suggests he should be good to go against the Falcons in Madrid this Sunday. Turner has started all seven games this season. He has 17 tackles, two forced fumbles and five passes defensed.
