stories.title: Bill Belichick again nominated for Pro Football Hall of Fame after controversial 2026 omission
stories.summary: The longtime Patriots head coach is eligible for the Hall of Fame for a second year.
stories.detailText: The Pro Football Hall of Fame is one step closer to righting some wrongs. After its selection committee controversially decided against longtime New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick in his first year of eligibility, the 74-year-old is now nominated for induction for a second year. Belichick is one of five former coaches announced as nominees by the Hall of Fame on Thursday. He is joined by Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan. Belichick spent time in Baltimore, Detroit and Denver before joining the New York Giants in 1979. He eventually helped the team win two Super Bowls as its defensive coordinator before departing for the Cleveland Browns. He later had stints with the Patriots and Jets before returning to New England via trade in 2000. With Belichick at the helm, the Patriots won a combined 69% 0f their regular season and playoff games between 2000 and 2023. A three-time NFL Coach of the Year winner, he left the organization with six Super Bowl wins, nine conference championships and 17 division titles under his belt. Including his tenure with the Browns, he ranks second all-time in NFL coaching wins with 333 and first with 31 postseason victories. Under normal circumstances, Belichick should be seen as the clear favorite to emerge past the next round of voting and eventually earn the famous golden jacket in the summer of 2027. However, as the 2026 voting process showed, anything is possible. In arguably the most controversial decision in the institution’s history, Belichick did not garner enough votes to clear the final hurdle — a decision that drew heavy criticism and raised questions about the integrity of the vote and those making the decisions. In the aftermath, the Hall of Fame announced sweeping changes to its process . The next step in Belichick’s Hall of Fame journey will come Nov. 17, when the committee will decide on one finalist to be presented to the full selection committee. The final vote will take place in early 2027, with the eventual Pro Football Hall of Fame class announced in the lead-up to the Super Bowl. Also among this year’s nominees is Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who is one of five contributors still in the running.

stories.title: Jonathan Taylor: No one likes uncertainty
stories.summary: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has spent the last two weeks fielding questions about whether he'll remain with the team and that will come to an end by next Tuesday one way or another.
stories.detailText: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor has spent the last two weeks fielding questions about whether he'll remain with the team and that will come to an end by next Tuesday one way or another. Taylor will either remain with the Colts through Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline or he'll be dealt to a team that thinks he can help push them over the top this season. Until he's dealt or the deadline passes, Taylor knows "you're not going to avoid" the questions he faced one again on Thursday and he knows that he'll be happy when they stop coming his way. "No one wants uncertainty ," Taylor said Thursday, via Stephen Holder of ESPN.com. "Until the past couple weeks, it's kind of been the same thing. But it won't be until Tuesday where you'll know exactly what's going on, you'll know exactly what the verdict is." Taylor played amid the rumors in last week's loss to the Jaguars and the plan is for him to play against the Cowboys this week. He said he is working to keep his focus on that game because he doesn't "want external factors creeping in and trying to alter your play," but that will be a much easier task to accomplish once there's certainty about where he'll be after November 10.

stories.title: Caleb Williams is a top-five NFL QB, and he’s doing it his way
stories.summary: Caleb Williams knows he can’t please everybody. But when you’re playing the way he is, his game speaks for itself. Check out @kdthompson5’s latest.
stories.detailText: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) leaves the field after defeating the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Heavy is the head that wears the crown. Caleb Williams has known that since well before the Chicago Bears made him the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, and it hasn’t fazed him in the slightest. Say what you want about him, he told reporters at Halas Hall on Wednesday. He’s just going to keep it pushing. “People are going to say what they have to say. I can’t please everybody. That’s not my job. My job is to go win games. My job is to be the best player I can be. My job is to believe in myself, trust in my teammates and go out there and be one of those guys on the field that makes game-changing plays. You like it, you don’t like it, you got to deal with it,” he said. Being an NFL quarterback, particularly one tasked with being the savior of a QB-starved franchise like the Bears, is no picnic. Add being a top pick and former Heisman Trophy winner with a penchant for showing his emotions and painting his nails to the mix, and even being objectively great at the game isn’t enough to get naysayers and trolls off your back. No matter. Because Williams has become a top-five quarterback in the NFL in his third season, and he’s done it by showing the doubters he can do what they said he couldn’t: the little things. A year after being a big-game hunter ( 9.2 average depth of target ) who struggled to consistently complete passes (58.1% completion rate), Williams has transformed himself into one of the most dangerous “game-managers” in the league (70.9% completion rate, second in the NFL behind Joe Burrow). Sure, he’s left some plays on the table and has dramatically lowered his ADOT compared to last year (6.8 in 2026), leading some to believe he’s become little more than a checkdown merchant. But if you watch with your eyes rather than box scores and passing charts, you see what Williams has truly become: a monster who’s capable of beating you any way at any time. caleb wyd pic.twitter.com/K7Jo4WpftV — frank (@realfrankbrank) November 4, 2026 Need him to take a checkdown to D’Andre Swift to make it 3rd-and-manageable or complete a 5-yard hot route to Colston Loveland for a first down? He’s got you. Want to see him rip a 25-yard strike down the middle of the field on a rope to a wide-open Luther Burden III or Rome Odunze, while evading an unblocked rusher? No problem. Playing chess with some of the best defenses in the NFL, including the Seattle Seahawks, like a conductor leading a symphony of offensive destruction? He’s got that in his bag, too. Williams’ second season in Ben Johnson’s offense, which currently sees him on pace to become the Bears’ first-ever 4,000-yard passer despite missing three games, has produced exactly the third-year leap teams beg for from their young quarterbacks. But it hasn’t been about constant fireworks, jaw-dropping downfield throws, and impossible sack evasions. It’s been about doing the boring, mundane stuff that all the greats will tell you wins championships. He’ll never be a guy that makes everyone happy. He’ll never be everything to everyone. But his game is rounding into one of the most complete skill sets in the league—whether the haters like it or not.

stories.title: Chiefs defense is looking in the mirror for a ‘killer instinct’
stories.summary: Kansas City’s defensive coordinator asked his unit to self-reflect after the fourth-quarter collapse in Denver.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the first play of the fourth quarter in Week 8, the Kansas City Chiefs converted a third down while leading 24-13 against the Denver Broncos . With a new set of downs and an 11-point lead, it felt like the game — and the AFC West lead — was in the Chiefs’ control. Three plays later, the Chiefs were punting away on fourth and inches, and nothing seemed to go right for Kansas City from there. We know the offense failed to finish the next two drives, both crucial possessions that could’ve put the game in the Chiefs’ favor. However, the defense allowed the Broncos to find their fourth-quarter magic, allowing two touchdowns in just 11 plays on the field. At his press conference on Thursday, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo described the loss as “sickening” before answering questions about the 28-24 defeat. “You have an 11-point lead going into the fourth quarter; the responsibility falls on the defense to make sure you win the game, and we didn’t do that,” Spagnuolo acknowledged. “I know that everyone wanted to score at the end. [Patrick Mahomes] has bailed us out a number of times in the eight years I’ve been here, but we don’t like to put the offense in that situation.” Leading into Denver’s nine-play touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs had forced three consecutive three-and-outs. In retrospect, with the defense giving way over the next two possessions, Spags had a message for his unit following the collapse. “I asked everybody to look in the mirror and ask themselves this question: Did we let up? Did we lose our edge? Did we lack the killer instinct?” “I think we all have to look at that,” Spags reflected. “Did I call it differently? Does it need to be called differently? And so we had that conversation, and hopefully we will be presented with that situation again.” While it may take self-reflection to finish these big games, the Chiefs are still looking for answers to finish plays, like opponent dropbacks. Kansas City is tied with the Miami Dolphins and New York Giants for the fewest sacks in the NFL. However, Chiefs defensive end George Karlafits leads the NFL in batted-down passes (7) after Week 8. For a team with a low sack total, that’s a silver lining worth pointing out for the coach. “I am happy with the six pass breakups,” Spagnuolo said. “When the offense drops back to throw the ball, all we’re concerned about is the end result. And quite frankly, sacks are glamorous… but on a third-down play, if a defensive lineman is knocking the ball down, you’re really getting the same thing: they’re punting.” “What would be really nice is if we could get some of those first- and second-down sacks when they throw it,” Spagnuolo acknowledged. While Spagnuolo’s point about early-down sacks helps, it seems that’s the only time the Chiefs get sacks this year. Out of the team’s nine sacks this season, only one has come on third down, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . Whether it’s a killer instinct needed or a better pass-rush plan, the Chiefs’ defense needs to finish more pass plays to the ground to help finish close games like last week’s in Denver.

stories.title: Hawks in the NFL: Week 8
stories.summary: There were some good performances from former Hawkeyes, but it was a scary week for one.
stories.detailText: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Amani Hooker #37 of the Tennessee Titans celebrates with teammates after intercepting quarterback Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images Apologies on my tardiness with this. I felt we needed a firm update on Jack Campbell before going forward with anything. We got a positive update from Campbell himself yesterday, so let’s go through a somber Week 8 in the NFL. Jack Campbell, TJ Hockenson, and Sam LaPorta Sunday started so well. We had a reunion in Detroit with two of the best tight ends the Hawks have produced in the last ten years plus an All-Pro in Campbell. Hockenson found the end zone again, his third touchdown of the year, in a 4-reception, 58-yard day. LaPorta finished with 1 carry for 2 yards plus 3 receptions for 33 yards as Detroit handed Minnesota their first loss of the season, 19-15. None of that matters at all, as Campbell was left severely injured in the fourth quarter trying to tackle Hockenson. I won’t link to the tackle. No need. You probably all saw it once and you don’t need to see it again. Campbell was motionless on the field for over 10 minutes, leaving his teammates clearly affected and in tears. Then led to the speculation and fear phase of this. No one knew what was going on with Campbell. Forget his playing career – will he be able to lead a normal life? That’s all that matters here. News was sparse and updates from the Lions were uncertain. Then we heard from Campbell himself and WHEW…some positive news! STATEMENT FROM JACK CAMPBELL My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express. I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such… — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 4, 2026 That’s about as good an update as we can get. Again, I don’t care about his playing career. If Campbell plays again, it’s a bonus. That is a great update and it sounds like he’ll be ok. We’ll keep an eye out for more updates on Campbell as they’re provided. Amani Hooker The big standout this week was Hooker. He’s stuck with this bad 1-7 Tennessee team (to their credit, they’ve shown proof of life at times this season.) And going to Cincinnati, that felt like a blow out was on the schedule for the Titans. They hung and lost in overtime, 43-36, and they hung in part due to Hooker. He finished with 6 tackles and 3 passes defended. He intercepted all 3 passes he defended. Amani Hooker has THREE interceptions this game on Burrow 🔥 TENvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PuBwu3Kt9z — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Those picks were worth a little scratch for Hooker. Nice bonus! And we still have a lot of football left this year. Can he get to six picks? Amani Hooker’s three-interception game off Joe Burrow is pay off – literally. Hooker earns $250,000 with at least four interceptions. He now has five. Six or more interceptions earns him $500,000. — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 1, 2026 Drew Stevens A little love for Stevens this week, who’s finding a nice groove now in his rookie year. Stevens made 4 of 5 field goals in Washington’s win over Philadelphia Sunday night (can we get the NFC East out of primetime? Thanks…) That included this 56-yard bomb. DREW STEVENS IS GOOD FROM 56-YARDS THE ROOKIE FROM IOWA pic.twitter.com/zkWm4JiblL — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) November 2, 2026 Lukas Van Ness Another good week at the office for Hercules, as the Packers defensive end started Week 8 last Thursday with 6 tackles, 1 sack, and 1 tackle for loss in a 27-19 win over Carolina. Van Ness is now at 4.5 sacks on the season, which is a career-high. Tristan Wirfs We’ll finish with the big man. Did anyone watch this game? Tampa Bay defeated Atlanta, 16-0, in a rain-soaked day in Tampa. Tampa completed zero passes in the game, the first time an NFL team has won a game without completing a pass since 1974. Wirfs was instrumental in the run game, as the Bucs rushed for 324 yards in the win. Wirfs earned a PFF run block grade of 85.9. To the comments!

stories.title: Rams holding punt returner competition again
stories.summary: The job for Kyren Williams as a punter returner would be simple: Just catch the ball.
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams are looking for a new player to fair catch punts for the rest of the season. Sean McVay told reporters this week that Kyren Williams and Tutu Atwell are the leaders in the clubhouse to win a job that nobody really wants because it only comes with dire consequences and no upside. The Rams have already released two punt returners during this season in Xavier Smith and Alex Bachman. It’s not that Williams or Atwell are in danger of being released, but they also don’t have anything to gain and that’s why the only real outcome left is to simply make sure you don’t muff or fumble the punt. Sean McVay said Kyren Williams and Tutu Atwell are candidates to return punts. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 4, 2026 If you think that McVay is worried about Williams’ health on punt returns, you’re seeing this job the wrong way. All he’s going to do if he gets the job is throw his hand up in the air and make a fair catch. That’s the most that McVay can hope for at this point after years of stumbling through special teams additions. Williams has six career punt returns in the NFL and an average of 6.6 yards per return. He had 14 punt returns in his final year at Notre Dame. There’s no hope of breaking one off for 60 yards. This is a “fair catch” job only. Atwell had 10 punt returns in 2021 and four punt returns in college. He’d only be out there to fair catch the ball. Ronnie Rivers is set to be activated this week and he has more extensive college returning experience than either of those players. He would also just fair catch the punt. Rams RB Ronnie Rivers is back to practice today. He’ll be activated this week and will return to the No. 3 RB role with special teams duty, too. He’s an option at kick returner. — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) November 4, 2026 Brennan Presley and Bachman (re-signed a day after he was released) would also be options from the practice squad. What would be their assignment if McVay asked them to return punts? Fair catch. That’s all the job is. Don’t muff. Let’s see who can handle it.

stories.title: Three former NY Giants head coaches have been nominated for the Pro Football Hall Of Fame
stories.summary: Three former NY Giants head coaches have been nominated for the Pro Football Hall Of Fame
stories.detailText: New York Giants head coach Tom Coughlin celebrates with the Vince Lombardi Trophy Three former New York Giants head coaches headline the Coaches Subcommittee’s ballot for the 2027 Hall Of Fame class. Tom Coughlin, Bill Belichick, and Dan Reeves, along with Mike Shannahan and Mike Holmgren, make up this year’s Head coach nominees for induction into the Pro Football Hall Of Fame . Giants’ fans will obviously have a soft spot for Coughlin, who was the Giants’ head coach from 2004 to 2015, winning two Super Bowls over that span. He was also the Jacksonville Jaguars’ first head coach, coaching them from 1995 to 2002. He took the Jaguars to the AFC Championship game in 1996 (their second season in existence) and again in 1999 on the strength of a 14-2 season. He was named Coach Of The Year following the 1996 season and Coughlin has the distinction of being one of just two coaches to beat fellow nominee Bill Belichick in the Super Bowl — and did so twice. Belichick was a coach for the Giants from 1979 to 1990, coaching special teams and linebackers before being named defensive coordinator by Bill Parcells in 1985. Belichick made his name as one of the NFL’s keenest defensive minds, and his gameplan from the Giants’ win over the Buffalo Bills in Super Bowl 25 is already in the Hall Of Fame. Belichick went on to be the head coach of the Cleveland Browns and New York Jets, but found almost unprecedented success with the New England Patriots. There he won six championships, tied for the most all time, but was also plagued by scandal. Dan Reeves coached the Giants from 1993 to 1996, and was named AP Coach Of The Year following the Giants’ 11-5 record. His subsequent seasons weren’t nearly as successful, but Reeves was one of the most successful coaches in NFL history. He’s one of just 13 head coaches to win (at least) 200 games between his time with the Denver Broncos (1981 to 1992), Giants (1993-1996), and Atlanta Falcons (1997 – 2003). Reeves passed away on January 1, 2022. Only one head coach can be inducted into the Hall Of Fame each year, and the former Giants’ coaches face stiff competition from Mike Holmgren and Mike Shanahan.

stories.title: The Chiefs welcome the Jets to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday with both teams desperate for a win
stories.summary: — The Kansas City Chiefs started the season with five straight wins, nearly matching their total from all of last season, when their run of three consecutive Super Bowl appearances came crashing down with a forgettable six-win campaign.
stories.detailText: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — The Kansas City Chiefs started the season with five straight wins, nearly matching their total from all of last season, when their run of three consecutive Super Bowl appearances came crashing down with a forgettable six-win campaign. Given such a debacle, it's not surprising the past two weeks have given some Kansas City folks an uneasy feeling . The Chiefs were waylaid in Seattle by the defending Super Bowl champions in a game that was never close, then went to Denver and blew an 11-point fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss last Sunday that gifted the Broncos the top spot in the AFC West. “We've still right there, 5-2, and we've won a lot of football games. Everything is out in front of us,” countered Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who has been playing at a high level less than 11 months after tearing ligaments in his left knee. "We just have to be better than we were last week and try to win a game," Mahomes said. The Chiefs would have a hard time finding a better get-right opponent than the Jets on Sunday . New York (2-6) has lost three straight , each a one-possession affair, and has struggled to stop anybody. And to make matters worse, star wide receiver Garrett Wilson was in the concussion protocol this week, offsetting the good news of the potential return of running back Breece Hall from a quadriceps injury that has sidelined him for the past five games. “We know exactly who this team is, we know exactly what they’re about,” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. “They’ve created a sustainable winning situation over there. That’s a lot of credit to the players, the coaching staff and the organization.” In short, the Chiefs represent the blueprint for what the Jets have spent years trying to achieve. “Your record is your record regardless of what your roster is,” Glenn said, "and that’s the way that I look at it. We just have to keep fighting and keep having that hunger to try to finish these games. A lot of that comes with what we’ve talked about, of having that killer instinct. When we’re up, of being able to take a team out. When we’re down, being able to fight our way in to be able to get ourselves back into position. When you look at it, we’ve done that.” The Chiefs have spent the past week searching for that same killer instinct. After beating the Broncos in their season opener, the Chiefs had an opportunity last week to take control of the AFC West before reaching the midway point of the season. But their problems in short-yardage situations, another miss by kicker Harrison Butker , and tackling woes on the defensive side of the ball ultimately doomed Kansas City to a frustrating defeat. “When you have losses — critical losses — early in the year, especially with this one, it's about finishing,” Chiefs pass rusher George Karlaftis said. “When you're up in the fourth quarter and you lose, it's on the defense. I know I felt it. I know the defense felt it. "Scheme aside, I think that mindset of finishing on every single play and never letting up, I think that will benefit us greatly.” Need to know New York Jets (2-6) at Kansas City (5-2). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS. Latest odds: Chiefs by 10. Against the spread: Jets 4-3-1; Chiefs 3-4. Last week: Jets lost to Raiders 38-33; Chiefs lost to Broncos 28-24. Last meeting: Chiefs beat Jets 23-20 on Oct. 1, 2023, in New York. Series record: Chiefs lead 21-19-1. Matchup to watch Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker against the Jets defensive front. Walker started the season on a tear, but was held to 36 yards rushing by Seattle and 69 yards by Denver. He'll have a chance to bounce back against a Jets defense that allowed the Bears to run for 232 yards, the Dolphins to run for 156 and the Patriots to run for 148 against it. Stats and stuff — The Chiefs' Emmett Johnson had 128 yards receiving last week in Denver, the most by a rookie running back in franchise history. — Kansas City has won three straight against the Jets at Arrowhead Stadium, outscoring them by an 83-22 margin. — Chiefs TE Travis Kelce will be playing his 200th game on Sunday. — Harrison Butker has missed 16 kicks since the start of last season for Kansas City, the most of any kicker in the NFL. — DT Chris Jones needs two sacks to pass Tamba Hali (89 1/2) for the second most in Chiefs history. — The Jets have been outscored 107-9 in the final two minutes of the first half in 25 games with Glenn as their coach. — New York was 2 of 6 scoring touchdowns in the red zone against Las Vegas last week. The Raiders were 4 for 4 in such situations. — Jets WR Adonai Mitchell had a breakout game with seven catches for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. — Jets RB Braelon Allen ran for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas. — The Jets scored on their first six possessions — two TDs, four field goals — in their loss to the Raiders. They joined the 2019 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (against the Giants) are the only teams since 2000 to lose after scoring on their first six possessions. ------ AP Football Writer Dennis Waszak in Florham Park, New Jersey, contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

Raiders owner Mark Davis is "not a fan" of gambling on sports
teamStories.summary: It's fitting that the owner of the team headquartered in the nation's gambling capital doesn't like gambling on sports.
teamStories.detailText: It's fitting that the owner of the team headquartered in the nation's gambling capital doesn't like gambling on sports. “I’m not a fan per se of gambling on sports , especially the one-on-ones, the proposition types of betting,” Raiders owner Mark Davis told Mike Ozanian of CNBC. “I think the key thing is the integrity of the game." Indeed it is. The integrity of the game — and the perception of integrity. “People have to believe in the game,” Davis said. “Is it worth the risk? I don’t know. I can’t answer that.” I can. It's not worth it. Back when the NFL hated gambling (before it realized how much money it could make by jumping in bed with the sports books), Commissioner Roger Goodell said this: ‘If gambling is permitted freely on sporting events, normal incidents of the game such as bad snaps, dropped passes, turnovers, penalties, and play calling inevitably will fuel speculation, distrust, and accusations of point-shaving or game-fixing." Now that sports gambling and prediction markets premised on sports outcomes have proliferated, there's a constant undercurrent of suspicion that the fix is in. The NFL can pretend all it wants that it's not happening, but it is. As long as it's not impacting the bottom line, the NFL will continue to look the other way. One big scandal could change that, permanently. For now, Davis is pragmatic, and candid, about the ensuing tension. “The revenue that is coming from gambling and those types of entities is large so there has to be a balance between integrity and . . . the good things that it can bring to the league,” Davis said. The only "good things" are money. Directly from the deals with sports books and the ability of owners to hold up to five percent of the equity in companies that operate sports books. And indirectly from the enhanced ratings that come from viewers who have action on a given game or the players in that game. The indirect benefits were always there, even when gambling was illegal in all states except the state where Davis's team plays. They would still be there if the NFL were to resume its hard line against gambling in all forms. But it's too late for that. The money is baked into the budgets. And the NFL isn't about to give up a viable revenue stream with which it has become fully accustomed.

teamStories.title: The Raiders make their return to the Bay Area when they take on the 49ers
teamStories.summary: — Maxx Crosby is one of the few remaining players on the Raiders with ties to the team's old home in Oakland, making this week's trip to play the
teamStories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — Maxx Crosby is one of the few remaining players on the Raiders with ties to the team's old home in Oakland, making this week's trip to play the San Francisco 49ers extra special. The Raiders (4-4) will play their first regular-season game in the Bay Area since moving from Oakland to Las Vegas after the 2019 season when they visit the 49ers (6-1) on Sunday. Crosby is one of three remaining Raiders who played in Oakland — along with tackle Kolton Miller and punter AJ Cole — and looks forward to the chance to play in front of some of those old fans who still travel to some of their games. “I know definitely being in the Bay, there’s going to be a lot of tension in the air and a lot excitement at the same time,” said Crosby, who was a rookie in the Raiders' last season in Oakland in 2019. “It’s special just being a part of that rivalry and just knowing the history, taking your time to really understand what that comes from and how important it was to all the fans.” The teams have met once since the Raiders moved with San Francisco winning 37-34 in overtime in Las Vegas in Week 17 of the 2022 season. The previous time they played in the Bay came in 2018 when the Niners won 34-3 in a Week 9 game played between a pair of one-win teams going nowhere. There's much more optimism this time with the 49ers at the top of the NFC standings despite losing their first game two weeks ago in Atlanta before a bye week and the Raiders coming in with a .500 record after beating the New York Jets last week. That will only add to the intensity for both the players and the fans of both teams, who still harbor animosity over the decades of sharing a home market. “It’s exciting for me because I know it’s exciting for the fans,” San Francisco linebacker Fred Warner said. “I’ve had several people on the outside tell me, man, y’all better beat the Raiders. So it means a lot even though they aren’t in Oakland anymore this week. They’re the Oakland Raiders this week, and so it’s an exciting man. I know it’ll be packed in there.” Need to know Las Vegas (4-4) vs. San Francisco (6-1) When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: 49ers by 9 1/2. Against the spread: Raiders 6-2; 49ers 4-3. Last week: Raiders beat the New York Jets 38-33; 49ers had bye, lost 29-20 to Atlanta on Oct. 25. Last meeting: 49ers beat Raiders 37-34 in OT on Jan. 1, 2023, in Las Vegas. Series record: 49ers lead 8-7. Matchup to watch Raiders TE Brock Bowers vs. 49ers pass defense. San Francisco allowed 18 catches for 127 yards by tight ends the past two weeks and now must match up with one of the game's best in Bowers. Bowers is the first tight end with at least 70 yards receiving in his first six games in a season and his 217 career catches are four shy of Trey McBride 's record for a tight end in his first three seasons. Stats and stuff — The Raiders have scored 89 more points through eight games than last season. First-year coach Klint Kubiak is the fourth coach since the merger in 1970 to register that kind of improvement as well as four or more victories. The others were the Baltimore Colts’ Ted Marchibroda in 1978, Los Angeles Rams’ Sean McVay in 2017 and Chicago’s Matt Nagy in 2018. — Kirk Cousins is the first Raiders quarterback with at least 2,000 yards passing (2,124) and 20 total touchdowns passing and running in the first eight games of a season. — The 221 points scored this season by the Raiders are tied for their fourth-most ever through eight games and most since 2002. The 230 points allowed are the fourth most for the franchise in the first eight games. — Las Vegas has allowed at least 30 points in five straight games, one shy of the longest streak ever in one season. — The Raiders have allowed a league-worst 6.1 yards per play this season, while the Niners have gained a league-high 6.4 yards per play. — The 49ers have won six of their past seven regular-season games coming off a bye week with their only loss in 2021 against Indianapolis. — Brock Purdy has 99 TD passes in 56 games and can become the fastest 49ers QB to 100 TD passes, breaking Frankie Albert's mark of 65 games. — San Francisco RB Christian McCaffrey has scored a touchdown in six straight games. He can become the 12th player ever with 50 games with at least 100 yards and one TD from scrimmage. — The 49ers have won 32 straight games in the regular season and playoffs when not committing a turnover, tied for the third-longest streak since 1939. — San Francisco had no takeaways and no sacks in its previous game, marking the 10th time that has happened in the past 10 seasons. ------ AP Sports Writer Mark Anderson contributed to this report ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

What has gone right -- and wrong -- for 10 new NFL head coaches in 2026 season
teamStories.summary: There are 10 new head coaches in the NFL this season, which ties the most ever. How are things going for each of them after eight weeks?
teamStories.detailText: The 2026 NFL offseason featured 10 head coaching changes, which tied with 1978, 1997, 2006 and 2022 for the most ever in an offseason, per ESPN Research. The Raiders hired Klint Kubiak after his Super Bowl win as the Seahawks' offensive coordinator. Three AFC North teams -- the Browns (Todd Monken), Steelers (Mike McCarthy) and Ravens (Jesse Minter) -- also changed coaches. Elsewhere in the AFC, the Bills promoted offensive coordinator Joe Brady to head coach, the Dolphins hired former Packers DC Jeff Hafley, and the Titans brought in Robert Saleh. In the NFC, Mike LaFleur, Kevin Stefanski and John Harbaugh were hired by the Cardinals, Falcons and Giants, respectively. How have these new coaches fared at their new destinations? We called on our NFL Nation reporters to evaluate both the positive and concerning signs from each team so far. Then, we provided a key stat on each team's start. The 10 teams with new coaches are listed below by ESPN Football Power Index 's playoff odds. We'll start in Western New York. Jump to a team: ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CLE LV | MIA | NYG | PIT | TEN Joe Brady, Buffalo Bills Record: 6-1 FPI chance to make playoffs: 99.4% What has gone right this season: Brady's offense, and his partnership with quarterback Josh Allen , is working. The Bills lead the NFL in points per game (33.3) and rank second in both yards per game and yards per play. The trade for wide receiver DJ Moore in the spring has made the Bills' offense more vertical, with Allen leading the NFL in yards per pass attempt (8.7). And their red zone rushing attack, led by Allen and RB James Cook III , has them converting red zone trips into touchdowns at a 70% clip. What has gone wrong this season: The pass defense has been a mess. The Bills have already moved on from safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson and benched cornerback Maxwell Hairston . Nickelback Dee Alford has been in and out of the lineup with injuries . Now, the Bills are relying on a rookie and a couple of players who started the season on the practice squad to take significant snaps for a unit that ranks 30th in yards allowed per game. -- Nick Suss, Bills reporter Key stat to know: This is the second time in the past 30 seasons that Buffalo has started 6-1 or better. The last such start was in 2022, when it finished 13-3 and lost to the Bengals in the divisional round of the playoffs. -- ESPN Research Mike McCarthy, Pittsburgh Steelers Record: 6-2 FPI chance to make playoffs: 81.0% What has gone right this season: A Pittsburgh native, McCarthy took the job with a special understanding of the core identity of the team. Halfway through his first season, he has upheld that in a big way. Led by running back Jaylen Warren and a young core of offensive linemen, the Steelers' offense is a physical unit capable of creating explosive plays in the run game. Defensively, McCarthy brought in coordinator Patrick Graham to reinforce those classic principles with his 3-4 front. The Steelers have held opponents to a league-best 51.3 rushing yards per game in the past three games. What has gone wrong this season: While McCarthy was brought in to maximize quarterback Aaron Rodgers , the passing game still lacks consistency. The Steelers rank 20th in passing yards per game (210.5) and 21st in air yards per attempt (6.5). And it's not all on Rodgers. Top receiver DK Metcalf has been plagued by drops, including one this past Sunday that resulted in an interception. The strong run game has carried the offense in the open field, but the Steelers are scoring touchdowns on only 50% of their red zone trips (tied for 26th in the NFL). Part of the problem is the playcalling. In the past four games, the Steelers utilized designed runs on just 31% of plays in goal-to-go situations. -- Brooke Pryor, Steelers reporter Key stat to know: The Steelers have a 4-0 record at home in 2026, which is their first such start since going 6-0 at home in 2020. And McCarthy's offense has shown up at Acrisure Stadium, averaging 27.8 points per game there versus 17.3 on the road. -- ESPN Research John Harbaugh, New York Giants Record: 4-2-1 FPI chance to make playoffs: 47.0% What has gone right this season: A lot. The Giants have already matched their win total from 2025. They're clearly a more buttoned-up and fundamentally sound team after repping situational football endlessly in training camp. And they're 3-1-1 in one-score games after finishing 1-7 last season. The biggest gains have been made by their special teams (ranked eighth in EPA) and defense (ninth overall). Hiring defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has worked out, as Wilson has done a solid job with a group that isn't loaded with talent and lost its best player in edge rusher Brian Burns ( torn ACL ). They're allowing 46.5 fewer yards per game than last season. What has gone wrong this season: Injuries have hit the Giants hard. They lost Burns and starting quarterback Jaxson Dart ( left knee injury ), arguably the two most important players on each side of the ball, for the season. New York spent the spring and summer creating an offense that prioritizes the quarterback's legs and had to pivot. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy has made it work relatively well with Dart, Jameis Winston and now J.J. McCarthy . But the injuries still have the Giants working with limitations. Their quarterbacks are averaging 13.2 yards rushing per game since Dart's injury. -- Jordan Raanan, Giants reporter Key stat to know: After their Week 7 win over the Texans, the Giants became the favorites to win the NFC East (-150 on DraftKings), the first time since 2016 that has happened at any point during a season. That year, they finished 11-5 and lost in the wild-card round to the Packers. Todd Monken, Cleveland Browns Record: 5-3 FPI chance to make playoffs: 16.8% What has gone right this season: The Browns are the second-youngest team in the NFL but have taken on a gritty, resilient persona behind Monken to help them dominate late-game situations. All five of Cleveland's wins have been courtesy of game-winning drives. "Coach Monk has put us in these situations in practice time after time ... so whenever we get into the game and whenever we get into these situations, we already have the confidence to go down there and set up a game-winning drive," rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion said. What has gone wrong this season: The offense -- Monken's area of expertise -- remains a work in progress. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has raised his level of play this season but still ranks 28th out of 30 qualifying players in QBR, and he could miss Week 9 after being put in concussion protocol . Inconsistent play from a new-look offensive line has also contributed to an offense that ranks 29th in points per game (17.4). "It's been a little bit of an up-and-down challenge," Monken said. "But that's part of the NFL, right? That's part of when you play the best in the world as you're trying to find your way, your footing, your players, coaches, schematically, to be consistent." -- Daniel Oyefusi, Browns reporter Key stat to know: Monken's team has already surpassed the Browns' win total from 2024 (three) and is one win away from beating Cleveland's 2025 total. Before Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Cleveland's four straight wins in division games (dating back to last season) were its longest streak since 1987. -- ESPN Research Klint Kubiak, Las Vegas Raiders Record: 4-4 FPI chance to make playoffs: 10.7% What has gone right this season: Despite the Raiders having an insufficient run game and weak WR room, they rank sixth in points per game (27.6) and 12th in total yards (342.4). That's because the dynamic between Kubiak and veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins has orchestrated one of the league's best passing games. Kubiak has been a good play designer, while Cousins' knowledge of the system has allowed him to execute those calls at a high rate. Cousins is third in passing yards (2,124) and second in touchdowns (19). Cousins' performance under center has led to the Raiders playing well on third down. Las Vegas has the 10th-best third-down conversion rate (41.7%). What has gone wrong this season: The Raiders cannot run the ball or stop the run. They are 31st in yards per attempt (3.0), 30th in rushing first downs (36) and last in yards before first contact (1.22). Las Vegas has been held to fewer than 100 rushing yards in six of its past seven games. Defensively, the Raiders are allowing opponents to run over them at a high rate. They have given up 146.4 rushing yards per game. Part of that issue is the Raiders' interior defensive line. No one has emerged as a consistent run stopper, as the Raiders are 30th in run stop win rate by interior linemen (24.8%). -- Ryan McFadden, Raiders reporter Key stat to know: Before defeating the Jets in Week 8, the Raiders were the third team in the past 10 seasons to start 3-0 and lose its next four games. And if the Raiders continue to average 27.6 points per game, it would be their most in a single season since 2002, when they averaged 28.1 and reached Super Bowl XXXVII . -- ESPN Research Kevin Stefanski, Atlanta Falcons Record: 3-5 FPI chance to make playoffs: 7.7% What has gone right this season: The Falcons have been perhaps the league's strangest team. But there have been positives on offense, which is Stefanski's specialty. After quarterback Michael Penix Jr . returned from a torn ACL in Week 3, the Falcons led the NFL in points per game in that span (31.0). Last season, Atlanta was 24th in points per game (20.8). The biggest change Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees have made? Getting Penix to play more under center. In 2025, he was under center a league-low 2.7% of the time and in the pistol a league-high 52.1%. This season, he has been under center 49.1% of the time, the fifth-highest rate in the NFL. What has gone wrong this season: The Falcons followed up beating the previously undefeated 49ers by losing to the Buccaneers despite quarterback Baker Mayfield not completing a single pass. It was the first time since 1974 such a thing had happened. That Week 8 game was played in a driving rain, and the entire thing might have been an anomaly. But Stefanski said in his introductory news conference that he wants Atlanta to run the football effectively and stop the run. The Bucs outrushed the Falcons 324-99 in that matchup. So Atlanta is still struggling with finding its identity. -- Marc Raimondi, Falcons reporter Key stat to know: The NFC South race is the most wide-open division race this late in the season since 2015 after the Panthers, Falcons and Buccaneers all took turns as favorites during Week 8. Atlanta could emerge from the group if it slows down on turnovers, as its 16 are the second most in the NFL and its most through eight games since 2003. -- ESPN Research Jesse Minter, Baltimore Ravens Record: 4-4 FPI chance to make playoffs: 6.4% What has gone right this season: Not much, quite honestly. When the Ravens started 4-1 -- tying the best start in team history -- Minter had the Ravens looking like a Super Bowl contender and had quarterback Lamar Jackson playing like an MVP again. With the creativity of first-year playcaller Declan Doyle, Baltimore ranked No. 6 in scoring (29.2 points per game) and No. 5 in yards (394.2) after five weeks. But injuries to Jackson caused everything to crumble. "It's definitely my job to make sure that we stay together, that we don't point fingers, that we have each other's back, that we believe in the next-man-up mentality," Minter said. The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett , so maybe that helps. What has gone wrong this season: The obvious answer is the loss of Jackson, who has played 14 full quarters this season because of injuries to his ankle and right thumb . But, beyond Jackson's injuries, the biggest disappointment has been the continued second-half collapses. From the time he was hired, Minter's mantra has been: "Be your best when your best is required." But he has failed to get the Ravens to finish games, which was one of the reasons why former coach John Harbaugh was fired. Baltimore held double-digit leads in three of its four losses this season. "There's something there that's missing," linebacker Roquan Smith said of the second-half flops. -- Jamison Hensley, Ravens reporter Key stat to know: The Ravens have been held to fewer than 14 points in three straight games, which hasn't been done since Weeks 1-4 in 2005. That team went 6-10, allowing them to land defensive tackle Haloti Ngata with the 12th pick of the 2006 draft. -- ESPN Research Mike LaFleur, Arizona Cardinals Record: 3-5 FPI chance to make playoffs: 1.1% What has gone right this season: When the offense works, it really works, showing off LaFleur's offensive ingenuity and playcalling. Granted, that hasn't happened often through eight games. When Arizona's offense gets rolling, it's easy to see the vision LaFleur has for his scheme because it can eat up yards and move downfield in a hurry. And it's clear how LaFleur wants to use his skill players, like wide receiver Michael Wilson and tight end Trey McBride , in those situations. It's just getting the offense to the point where it's rolling that has been an issue. What has gone wrong this season: The list is long and mighty. Injuries have decimated Arizona's skill positions with RB Jeremiyah Love ( high ankle sprain ) and WR Kendrick Bourne (tibia) going on IR. The Marvin Harrison Jr . experiment under LaFleur didn't work out, so they traded him to Houston . The red zone offense came to a screeching halt recently. And the Cardinals changed quarterbacks at the end of Sunday's game. More has gone wrong than right this season for LaFleur. Key stat to know: LaFleur's team is 3-0 this season as an underdog of seven-plus points ( 7 at Cowboys , 8.5 at Chargers and 13.5 at Rams ), which is tied with 11 others for second-most since 1966. The record of 4-0 was set by the 1933 Bears. -- ESPN Research Jeff Hafley, Miami Dolphins Record: 1-6 FPI chance to make playoffs: What has gone right this season: Their rookie class is making an early impact. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez is a contender for Defensive Rookie of Year, ranking sixth in the NFL in tackles per game. And despite their record, the Dolphins have also shown fight in most games this season -- even after losing running back De'Von Achane , their best player, to an ACL injury in Week 2 . This season is more about development than wins and losses, and Miami's young core is starting to take shape. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, rookies have accounted for more than a quarter of the team's defensive snaps this season. What has gone wrong this season: The aforementioned season-ending injury to Achane left the team without its offensive focal point and one of its captains. The Dolphins also blew a two-score halftime lead to the Patriots and lost winnable games to the Vikings and Chiefs . Quarterback Malik Willis has shown development over the first half of the season, but he has yet to reach the same level of production and efficiency he showed in limited action with Green Bay. Miami's pass rush wasn't expected to be anywhere close to the league's best, but it has been one of the league's worst with an NFL-low nine sacks. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques, Dolphins reporter Key stat to know: Miami currently has a 29% chance at the No. 1 pick in the 2027 draft, according to ESPN's Football Power Index. That's second behind the Titans (39%) and would increase to 34% with a loss to the Lions in Week 9 . -- ESPN Research Robert Saleh, Tennessee Titans Record: 1-7 FPI chance to make playoffs: What has gone right this season: Saleh has done a really good job navigating some adverse situations , which most recently was the trade of franchise cornerstone Jeffery Simmons . Saleh's message to those remaining on the roster was a challenge to take advantage of the opportunity created by the Simmons trade. Despite losing their clear team leader, the Titans took the high-powered Bengals to overtime and forced a season-high four turnovers. It would be easy to point fingers or splinter apart, but Saleh has the Titans fighting every week. "These guys are resilient, man," Saleh said. "They've seen it all. Once the initial shock is over and we get to the grass, the world kind of goes away." What has gone wrong this season: Tennessee has not figured out how to win close games, with a 1-5 record in games decided by one score (eight points) or less. Quarterback Cam Ward has led multiple drives to take a lead in the fourth quarter, but the defense allowed game-winning drives to the Eagles, Browns and Bengals. Conversely, when the defense set the offense up for a game-winning drive against the Giants, Ward threw a crushing interception in New York's end zone. "I feel like I stand up here every week and say the same thing," Saleh said after the 43-36 loss to the Bengals last Sunday. "We've gotta figure it out, the end-of-game situations." -- Turron Davenport, Titans reporter Key stat to know: The Titans have trailed at halftime in every game this season, including four matchups where they scored first. They have had consecutive 1-7 or worse starts, which is their worst since three straight from 1982 to 1984. -- ESPN Research

teamStories.title: Las Vegas Raiders’ defense must find answers for San Francisco 49ers Kyle Juszczyk packages in Week 9 key matchups
teamStories.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are in the AFC playoff picture with a 4-4 record heading into Week 9, but the Raiders haven’t proven they can beat a playoff-caliber team yet. Facing off against the NFC-leading 6-1 San Francisco 49ers this Sunday is a great opportunity for Las Vegas to announce itself as a legitimate postseason …
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are in the AFC playoff picture with a 4-4 record heading into Week 9, but the Raiders haven’t proven they can beat a playoff-caliber team yet. Facing off against the NFC-leading 6-1 San Francisco 49ers this Sunday is a great opportunity for Las Vegas to announce itself as a legitimate postseason contender by winning the three key matchups below and the game. Raiders’ Defense vs. Juszczyk Packages While fullbacks have become less common in modern NFL offenses, Kyle Juszczyk has become one of many valuable weapons in Kyle Shanahan’s offense over the years. In 2026, the 49ers have leaned on 21 personnel more than any other personnel package, leading the league with a 34.5% rate (6.6% more than any other team) and 141 total plays (22 more plays than any other team), per Sumer Sports . Unsurprisingly, San Francisco also tops the charts in total EPA (11.21) when using 21 personnel, according to Sumer. While Shanahan’s crew dips to eighth in EPA per play (0.08), all of the teams ahead of them have 10 or fewer plays in those packages this season. Additionally, they are one of two offenses to have a positive EPA per pass (0.05, ranks 13th) and per rush (0.1, sixth) in 21 personnel. The New York Jets are the other club, and the Jets have just four plays with that grouping on the field. Juszczyk’s unique skill set allows the 49ers to lean so heavily on these packages. While his 58.8 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus might seem low, that ranks fourth among fullbacks with at least 27 run blocks and is only 1.8 points behind the position’s leader, Adam Prentice (60.6) from the Denver Broncos. Additionally, Prentice has less than a third of the run-blocking snaps that Juszczyk has (30 to 99). On top of that, of running backs who have at least 20 carries with 21 personnel on the field, San Francisco’s Kaelon Black has the highest yards per carry (4.52) and Christian McCaffrey is second (4.49), per Sumer . Meanwhile, the Raiders’ defense has only seen 27 rushes against 21 personnel, but ranks dead last in EPA per rush allowed (0.133) and 28th in success rate (48.1%). Additionally, the fullback’s impact extends to the passing game. He has a modest eight catches for 76 yards and two touchdowns, but the pair of scores highlights how he needs to be accounted for as a receiver in the red zone. Also, of tight end George Kittle’s 34 catches and 425 yards this season, nine catches (26.5%) and 139 yards (32.7%) have come in 21 personnel, and all nine grabs are charted as “impact plays” by Sumer . Las Vegas is closer to the middle of the pack when it comes to defending the passing game against said packages, ranking 15th in EPA per pass (negative 0.104) and 19th in success rate (50%). However, the sample size is small with just 18 plays, and Shanahan doesn’t always use his fullback in the traditional sense. Per PFF , Juszczyk has lined up as a tight end or wide receiver (66 snaps inline, 45 in the slot and 17 out wide) more often than he has in the backfield (52 snaps) this season. That goes back to his versatile skill set, as Shanahan uses 21 personnel to run 12 personnel plays with the “fullback” and Kittle on the field at the same time. That’s been an issue for the Raiders’ coverage unit, facing 60 pass plays with two tight ends on the field and ranking 22nd in EPA per pass (0.169) and 20th in success rate (51.7%), according to Sumer . Additionally, the defense had a tough time against the New York Jets’ 12 personnel packages last week, giving up 0.32 EPA per pass and a 50% success rate , and 0.3 EPA per rush and a 57.1% success rate on the ground. So, whether Juszczyk is lined up as a traditional fullback or at tight end, the Silver and Black have to find answers when he’s on the field. Those packages are a big factor in the 49ers’ offense that ranks fourth with 28.1 points per game . Raiders’ IOL vs. 49ers’ Interior Pass-Rush (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images" data-portal-copyright="Getty Images" /> We’re essentially at the halfway point of the 2026 season, and it’s pretty clear that the Raiders are a passing offense. For context, they rank third in passing yards per game ( 265.1 ) and are second-worst in rushing yards per game (77.3). Diving even deeper into the efficiency metrics, the Silver and Black are sixth in EPA per pass (0.18) and second-to-last in EPA per rush (negative 0.24), according to Sumer . That’s led to a career resurgence for Kirk Cousins, who has the third-most passing yards ( 2,124 ) and second-most touchdowns (19) in the league through eight weeks. However, he’s a different quarterback when under pressure. With a clean pocket, PFF has Cousins with the 10th-best passing grade (88.4), tied for seventh in “big-time throws” (seven) and tied for the eighth-fewest “turnover-worthy plays” (two) out of 35 qualifying quarterbacks. However, those figures dip to 15th in passing grade (50.1), tied for 17th in BTTs (three) and tied for the 13th-most TWPs (five) when under pressure. That’s where the 38-year-old’s lack of mobility and arm strength show up. Meanwhile, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner will be making his return to San Francisco on Sunday after the club traded for him during the bye week. Buckner, who was the 49ers’ first-round pick in 2016 and spent four seasons with the team, has a reputation as one of the better interior pass-rushers in the league. In seven games with the Indianapolis Colts, he registered 20 pressures (tied for 16th among defensive tackles), per PFF , and four sacks this season. The 11-year pro also has three batted passes (tied for sixth) and a 73.7 pass-rush grade (17th) on the campaign. But San Francisco’s pass-rush goes beyond the new acquisition who hasn’t played a snap for the team yet. Osa Odighizuwa is 15th among defensive tackles in pressures (21), while rookie Gracen Halton has flashed on limited opportunities to post a 70.7 PFF pass-rush grade (27th). Those three could be problematic for the Raiders’ interior offensive line. Left guard Spencer Burford has surrendered the third-most pressures ( 19 ) and has the 10th-lowest pass-blocking grade (41.0) at his position, while right guard Trey Zuhn III will make just his second career start. Zuhn had a decent showing last week by yielding just two pressures on 27 opportunities, but the Jets don’t have nearly the same interior pass-rush as the 49ers do. Luckily, center Tyler Linderbaum should be able to help the two guards out. While the big-ticket free-agent signing has faced some scrutiny for not living up to his contract so far this season, that’s primarily due to the ground game, as he’s been stingy in pass protection. Linderbaum has surrendered just eight pressures on 307 opportunities and is 13th among centers with a 70.3 pass-blocking grade . For the record, he’s been better as a run-blocker over the last two weeks with back-to-back PFF run-blocking grades above the baseline (60.0) after being below it in four of the first six contests. Especially with edge rusher Nick Bosa missing the last five games with a calf injury — and potentially on a pitch count if he returns this week — San Francisco’s interior pass-rush figures to be a key factor on Sunday. Mayer vs. Warner Brock Bowers may draw the headlines in Las Vegas’ tight end room, but Bowers is used more like a wide receiver in Klint Kubiak’s offense. According to PFF , nearly 85% of his pass snaps have come either out wide or in the slot. As a result, Michael Mayer is the Raiders’ more traditional tight end, spending 72.5% of his pass snaps inline. Also, he’s having a career year. Eight games into the season, Mayer has already logged personal bests in catches (36) and receiving yards (351). Additionally, those figures rank fourth and ninth among tight ends , and one more receiving touchdown will match his previous single-season high with two. The fourth-year pro’s YAC ability — which accounts for 180 or 51.3% of his yardage total — has provided Cousins with a reliable check-down option in the passing game. Mayer has the seventh-most YAC at his position, is 22nd in YAC per reception (5.0) and has forced five missed tackles (tied for seventh), helping record the fourth-most first downs (22) among tight ends. However, he hasn’t faced a linebacker of Fred Warner’s caliber yet. The four-time first-team All-Pro has established himself as the best player at his position in the league, partially due to having a well-rounded skill set. In coverage this season, he ranks tied for third among linebackers with three forced incompletions, tied for fifth in forced incompletion rate (13%) and tied for 14th in coverage stops (10), per PFF . While Warner has yielded 98 of his 155 receiving yards after the catch and has four missed tackles at a 13.3% rate in coverage, that’s primarily come against running backs. According to Sumer , he’s surrendered just five catches for 37 total yards to tight ends in 2026, with a measly three yards coming with the ball in their hands. That sets up an interesting battle between him and Mayer. In the running game, Warner primarily lines up as an inside backer (265 out of 452 snaps or 58.6%), per PFF , where he’s taking on blocks from offensive linemen more often than not. But he has recorded 153 snaps (33.8%) as either an off-ball or line of scrimmage outside linebacker, where he’s more likely to draw tight ends in the running game. That could be a challenge for Mayer, whose 58.7 PFF run-blocking grade is tied for 46th among tight ends, and his five “impact blocks” from Sumer is tied for 19th at the position. Meanwhile, Warner leads linebackers with a 91.6 run defense grade , is tied for 13th in run stops (16) and is ninth in run-stop rate (10.1%). In other words, the Raiders’ tight end has to bring his ‘A-game’ on Sunday since he’ll likely see the 49ers’ best defender and the NFL’s top linebacker early and often.
